AGENCY:
Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice of application for exemption; request for comments.
SUMMARY:
FMCSA requests public comment on Amiran Morchiladze's application for an exemption or other temporary relief from the eligibility requirements related to immigration status that are applicable to the issuance of a non-domiciled commercial driver's license (CDL). Mr. Morchiladze requests temporary relief to allow him to renew or restore his non-domiciled CDL while his immigration case is pending. FMCSA is required by statute to publish a notice explaining each exemption request. This notice does not indicate what decision FMCSA will ultimately reach on the request. After reviewing the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted, FMCSA will grant or deny the exemption.
DATES:
Comments must be received on or before December 24, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments identified by Docket Number FMCSA-2026-3632 by any of the following methods:
Federal eRulemaking Portal:
www.regulations.gov
.
See the Public Participation and Request for Comments section below for further information.
Mail:
Dockets Operations, U.S. Department of Transportation, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, West Building, Washington, DC 20590-0001.
Hand Delivery or Courier:
1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, West Building, Washington, DC 20590-0001, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
Fax:
(202) 493-2251. Each submission must include the Agency name and the docket number (FMCSA-2026-3632) for this notice. Note that DOT posts all comments received without change to
www.regulations.gov
,
including any personal information included in a comment. Please see the Privacy Act heading below.
Privacy Act:
In accordance with
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)
, DOT solicits comments from the public to better inform its exemption process. DOT posts these comments, including any personal information the commenter provides, to
www.regulations.gov
,
as described in the system of records notice DOT/ALL-14 FDMS (Federal Docket Management System (FDMS)), which can be reviewed at
https://www.transportation.gov/​individuals/​privacy/​privacy-act-system-records-notices
.
The comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Ms. Bernadette Walker, FMCSA Driver and Carrier Operations Division; Office of Carrier, Driver and Vehicle Safety Standards;
Bernadette.walker@dot.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Public Participation and Request for Comments
FMCSA encourages you to participate by submitting comments and related materials.
A. Submitting Comments
If you submit a comment, please include the docket number for this notice (FMCSA-2026-3632), indicate the specific section of this document to which the comment applies, and provide a reason for your suggestions or recommendations. You may submit your comments and material online or by fax, mail, or hand delivery, but please use only one of these means. FMCSA recommends that you include your name and a mailing address, an email address, or a phone number in the
(
printed page 75965)
body of your document so the Agency can contact you if it has questions regarding your submission.
To submit your comment online, go to
https://www.regulations.gov/​docket/​FMCSA-2026-3632/​document
,
click on this notice, click “Comment,” and type your comment into the text box on the following screen.
If you submit your comments by mail or hand delivery, submit them in an unbound format, no larger than 8
                    1/2
                     by 11 inches, suitable for copying and electronic filing.
FMCSA will consider all comments and material received during the comment period. Comments received after the comment closing date will be filed in the public docket and will be considered to the extent practicable.
B. Confidential Business Information (CBI)
CBI is commercial or financial information that is both customarily and actually treated as private by its owner. Under the Freedom of Information Act (
5 U.S.C. 552
), CBI is exempt from public disclosure. If your comments responsive to the notice contain commercial or financial information that is customarily treated as private, that you actually treat as private, and that is relevant or responsive to the notice, it is important that you clearly designate the submitted comments as CBI. Please mark each page of your submission that constitutes CBI as “PROPIN” to indicate it contains proprietary information. FMCSA will treat such marked submissions as confidential under the Freedom of Information Act, and they will not be placed in the public docket of the notice. Submissions containing CBI should be sent to Sarah Stella, Chief, Regulatory Development Division, Office of Policy, FMCSA, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, Washington, DC 20590-0001 or via email at
sarah.stella@dot.gov
.
At this time, you need not send a duplicate hardcopy of your electronic CBI submissions to FMCSA headquarters. Any comments FMCSA receives not specifically designated as CBI will be placed in the public docket for this notice.
C. Viewing Comments and Documents
To view comments, as well as any documents mentioned in this preamble as being available in the docket, go to
https://www.regulations.gov
,
insert FMCSA-2026-3632 in the keyword box, select the document tab and choose the document to review. To view comments, click this notice, then click “Browse Comments.” If you do not have access to the internet, you may view the docket by visiting Dockets Operations in the DOT West Building, 1200 New Jersey Avenue SE, W58-213, Washington, DC 20590-0001, between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, except Federal holidays.
II. Legal Basis
FMCSA has authority under
49 U.S.C. 31136(e)
and
31315(b)
to grant exemptions from the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSRs). FMCSA must publish a notice of each exemption request in the
Federal Register
(
49 CFR 381.315(a)
). The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analysis. The Agency must provide an opportunity for public comment on the request.
The Agency reviews the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted and determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption, pursuant to the standard set forth in
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1)
. The Agency must publish its decision in the
Federal Register
(
49 CFR 381.315(b)
). If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision(s) from which the exempted party will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (
49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)
). If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (
49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)
). The exemption may be renewed (
49 CFR 381.300(b)
).
III. Applicant's Request
Current Regulatory Requirements
On February 13, 2026, FMCSA published a final rule amending the Federal regulations for State Driver's Licensing Agencies (SDLAs) issuing commercial driving credentials to foreign-domiciled individuals, effective March 16, 2026 (
91 FR 7044
). Under
49 CFR 383.73(f)(3)(ii)(A)
, as amended, SDLAs must not issue non-domiciled commercial learner's permits or CDLs unless the applicant provides evidence of lawful immigration status, as defined under
49 CFR 383.5
. Section 383.5 provides that
evidence of lawful immigration status,
for applicants domiciled in foreign jurisdictions (other than U.S. territories), consists of an unexpired foreign passport and a Form I-94/94A issued by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security with an unexpired Admit Until Date indicating a classification of H-2A-Temporary Agricultural Workers, H-2B-Temporary Non-Agricultural Workers, or E-2-Treaty Investors.
Applicant's Request
Mr. Morchiladze states that he has lived in the United States for nearly 10 years. He states that his CDL expired on August 6, 2026 and that he is currently unable to renew his commercial driving privileges because of the applicable eligibility requirements related to immigration status. Mr. Morchiladze requests an individual exemption or other temporary relief that would allow him to renew or restore his non-domiciled CDL while his immigration case and application for adjustment of status are pending. He states that without relief he may lose his truck, the small business he has been building, and his primary source of income.
Applicant's Equivalent Level of Safety
Mr. Morchiladze asserts that granting the exemption would not reduce safety. He states that he completed CDL training and testing in English, passed all three portions of the CDL skills test on his first attempt, and has commercial driving experience operating box trucks, dry vans, flatbeds, Conestoga trailers, and step-deck equipment.
He further states that he has not received a traffic ticket or moving violation and that roadside and scale inspections have not resulted in violations or out-of-service orders. Mr. Morchiladze states that he is willing to satisfy additional safety requirements, including retaking knowledge or road tests, completing language testing, obtaining updated medical certification, and would permit additional review of his driving and inspection records.
A copy of Mr. Morchiladze's application for exemption is available for review in the docket for this notice.
IV. Request for Comments
In accordance with
49 U.S.C. 31315(b)
, FMCSA requests public comment from all interested persons on Mr. Morchiladze's application for an exemption or other temporary relief from the eligibility requirements related to immigration status affecting issuance or renewal of a non-domiciled CDL. All comments received before the close of business on the comment closing date will be considered and will be available for examination in the docket at the location listed under the
ADDRESSES
section of this notice. Comments received after the comment closing date will be filed in the public docket and will be considered to the extent practicable. In addition to late comments, FMCSA will also continue to file, in the public docket, relevant
(
printed page 75966)
information that becomes available after the comment closing date. Interested persons should continue to examine the public docket for new material.
Larry W. Minor,
Associate Administrator for Policy.

Needs and Uses:
The information collection requirement supported by these DD Forms supports contractor requirements to have government approval of contract flight crewmembers and contract flights as specified in Defense Contract Management Command Instruction (DCMA INST) 8210.1, Contractor's Ground and Flight Operations. The contractor provides information on contractor personnel to the government. The government approves the contractor's request for aircrew training and, eventually, approval for contractor personnel to operate and fly government aircraft. The government also approves all flights under contract.
The DD Form 2627 is used by contractors to request qualification training for contractor crewmembers. The contractor provides a personal history, verifies the crewmember's records, and requests government approval for training in a particular type of government aircraft. The 2627 and supporting documentation can be provided in hard or soft copy.
The DD Form 1821 is used by contractors to provide a succinct summary of a crewmember's flight history. This form is submitted along with DD Form 2627 as part of the supporting documentation for the request for qualification training.
The DD Form 2628 is used by contractors to request aircrew qualification for contractor crewmembers. The contractor verifies the crewmember's training completion and requests government approval for specific aircrew qualification in a particular type of government aircraft. The 2628 and supporting documentation can be provided in hard or soft copy.
The DD Form 3062 is used by contractors to request approval of flights under contract. The 3062 can be provided in hard or soft copy. Without the approval from the government, the contractor cannot fly under the liability coverage provided by DFARS 252.228-7001, Ground and Flight Risk.
Affected Public:

DD Forms 1821, 2627, and 2628 are completed once to verify a contractor's aircrew qualification. DD Form 3062 is completed as needed to request approval of flights under contract.

SUMMARY:
The Postal Service is revising
Mailing Standards of the United States Postal Service,
International Mail Manual (IMM®), to reflect changes to product features for Priority Mail International® (PMI) and to introduce International Proof of Delivery as a new international extra service that will be available for PMI mailpieces to select destinations.
DATES:
Effective:
January 17, 2027.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Michelle Lassiter at 202-268-9678.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
The 2025 Universal Postal Union (UPU) Dubai Congress amended the Universal Postal Convention (Convention) to establish a proof of delivery service for parcels that UPU-designated postal operators are required to offer for inbound parcels, effective January 1, 2027. However, the proof of delivery service for parcels is optional for outbound parcels. The Postal Service is introducing International Proof of Delivery for PMI items where the destination postal operator does not include evidence of delivery as a standard feature for their parcel service.
On August 21, 2026, the Postal Service filed a request with the Postal Regulatory Commission (PRC) to establish outbound International Proof of Delivery as a new International Ancillary Service in Docket No. MC2026-355. On September 16, 2026, in Order No. 9727, the PRC issued an order approving the classification changes conditioned upon the Postal Service filing a supplementary notice, which the Postal Service filed on November 12, 2026, in Docket No. MC2026-355. The order can be viewed on the Postal Regulatory Commission's website at
https://prc.gov
.
International Proof of Delivery is scheduled to go into effect, pending approval by the PRC of the price for International Proof of Delivery that is included in the notice concerning competitive published price changes that are to be effective January 17, 2027, which the Postal Service filed on November 12, 2026, in Docket No. CP2027-1.
The Postal Service will publish an appropriate update to Notice 123,
Price List,
and an appropriate amendment to
39 CFR part 20
to reflect these changes.

350 International Proof of Delivery
351 Description
International Proof of Delivery service is available at the time of mailing for Priority Mail International items where the destination postal operator does NOT include evidence of delivery as a standard feature of their parcel service. International Proof of Delivery provides evidence, upon request by the sender, that the item has been delivered to the addressee (or representative). The form of evidence could include at least one of the following:
a. A signature of acceptance.
b. Captured data from an identity card.
c. An electronic or written record from the recipient authorizing out-of-home delivery in advance.
d. An electronic or written record from the recipient accepting delivery without the recipient's presence.
e. Another form of proof of delivery that is legally binding under the legislation of the country of destination to confirm acceptance.
Note:
Restricted Delivery
service is no longer available for international mail—it was discontinued effective January 27, 2013.
352 Availability
International Proof of Delivery service can be obtained only at the time of mailing at a Post Office retail service counter, online using Click-N-Ship, through USPS APIs, or using USPS-produced Global Shipping Software (GSS). International Proof of Delivery service is available for Priority Mail International items destined to countries that do NOT provide proof of delivery as a standard feature of their parcel service. See Individual Country Listings for additional country-specific information.
353 Fee
See Notice 123,
Price List,
for the International Proof of Delivery fee. This fee must be paid in addition to postage and other applicable charges.
354 Processing Requests
354.1 Marking
All International Proof of Delivery items of U.S. origin must bear a customs form with a service indicator (
i.e.
barcode prefix) of within the range FA-FZ. Additionally, the Proof of Delivery symbol displayed in Exhibit 354.1 must appear on the customs form or non-removable sticker on the address side of the mailpiece.
354.2 Proof of Delivery Improperly Completed or Not Received
If the sender does not receive proof of delivery for which a fee was paid, an inquiry may be filed. See 920 for inquiry procedures.

This notice updates the November 4, 2026 notice announcing the appointment of members of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Senior Executive Service (SES) Performance Review Boards (PRBs) for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This notice updates the notice published on November 4, 2026 at
91 FR 69568
, to add one name to the FY 2026 SES PRBs for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The purpose of the PRBs is to make recommendations to the appointing authority (
i.e.,
Agency Head) on the performance of senior executives (career and limited term appointees), including recommendations on performance ratings, performance-based pay adjustments, and performance awards. The PRBs will also make recommendations on the performance of Transportation Security Executive Service, Senior-Level, and Scientific and Professional employees. To make its recommendations, the PRBs will review performance appraisals, initial summary ratings, any response by the employee, and any higher-level official's recommendation.
In accordance with
5 U.S.C. 4314(c)
and
5 CFR 430.311
, each agency must establish one or more PRBs to make recommendations to the appointing authority (
i.e.,
Agency Head) on the performance of its senior executives. Each PRB must consist of three or more members. More than one-half of the membership of a PRB must be SES career appointees when reviewing appraisals and recommending performance-based pay adjustments or performance awards for career appointees. Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106946; File No. SR-FINRA-2026-027]
November 20, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 18, 2026, the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by FINRA. FINRA has designated the proposed rule change as constituting a “non-controversial” rule change under paragraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 under the Act,
[
3
]
which renders the proposal effective upon receipt of this filing by the Commission. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
FINRA is proposing to amend FINRA Rule 11892 (Clearly Erroneous Transactions in Exchange-Listed Securities) in light of the Commission's approval of Overnight Protected Bands for 23/5 Trading.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on FINRA's website at
http://www.finra.org
and at the principal office of FINRA.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, FINRA included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. FINRA has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Background
In connection with the Commission's approval of proposals by multiple national securities exchanges to introduce trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week (“23/5 Trading”), the Operating Committee of the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility (“LULD Plan”)
[
4
]
filed proposed Amendment 27 to the LULD Plan, which proposed to establish price band protections during overnight trading hours (“Overnight Price Bands”).
[
5
]
The Operating Committee proposed that the Overnight Price Bands would initially be temporary static bands 20% above and below two reference points, and that after implementation, the Operating Committee would evaluate the performance of such Overnight Price Bands and propose appropriate changes in a new plan amendment.
[
6
]
On August 5, 2026, the Commission approved the proposal.
[
7
]
In light of the Commission's approval of these changes to the LULD Plan, including new Overnight Price Bands, FINRA now proposes several amendments to Rule 11892.
In general, Rule 11892 describes the process by which a FINRA officer may, on his or her own motion, review any over-the-counter transaction involving an exchange-listed security and declare any such transaction null and void if the officer determines that (A) the transaction is clearly erroneous or (B) such actions are necessary for the maintenance of a fair and orderly market or the protection of investors and the public interest, consistent with the guidelines set forth in the rule. The current rule's central premise is that, if LULD Price Bands under the LULD Plan were available and correct at the time the transaction was executed, the transaction is not eligible for clearly erroneous review. Specifically, Rule 11892(b)(1) currently provides that “[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during Normal Market Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous” except in certain limited circumstances, including when (A) the transaction is in an NMS Stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan (
e.g.,
rights and warrants), (B) the transaction was executed at a time when LULD Price Bands were not available, or resulted from a member's technology or systems issue that caused the transaction to occur outside the applicable LULD Price Bands, or was executed after the primary listing market declared a regulatory trading halt, suspension, or pause, or (C) several other limited circumstances.
[
8
]
In approving an exchange rule filing adopting substantively similar parameters in 2022, the Commission noted that restricting clearly erroneous review in this way during times when LULD Price Bands were in effect was “consistent with the Act and will
(
printed page 75957)
further the goal of providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Price Bands will stand and not be broken. . . . Thus, the proposal is designed to limit the potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review process.”
[
9
]
Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Normal Market Hours, meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Normal Market Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, FINRA now proposes to extend the restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place. This proposed change would be consistent with the Commission's rationale described above in approving the prior substantively similar exchange rule filing because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review during overnight trading hours, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken.
Proposed Change to Rule 11892(a)(1)
To implement this change, FINRA proposes to add several definitions to Rule 11892(a)(1). First, FINRA would add that the term “LULD Protected Hours” includes Normal Market Hours (9:30 a.m. Eastern Time (“E.T.”) to 4:00 p.m. E.T.) and Overnight Protected Hours, as defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan. Second, FINRA would define “LULD Price Bands” or “Price Bands” to mean the Price Bands defined in Section V of the LULD Plan (
i.e.,
the Price Bands that apply during Normal Market Hours) and “Overnight Price Bands,” as defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (
i.e.,
the Price Bands that apply to the Overnight Protected Hours from 9:00 p.m. E.T. through 4:00 a.m. E.T.).
[
10
]
FINRA proposes to amend Rule 11892(a) to replace the phrase “Normal Market Hours (9:30 a.m. Eastern Time to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time)” with “LULD Protected Hours,” to provide that a FINRA officer may, on his or her own motion, review any over-the-counter transaction involving an exchange-listed security occurring outside of LULD Protected Hours or eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (b)(1) of Rule 11892 arising out of or reported through a trade reporting system owned or operated by FINRA or FINRA Regulation and authorized by the Commission, provided that the transaction meets the guidelines set forth in Rule 11892. This change would extend the LULD-based restrictions on clearly erroneous review currently in place during Normal Market Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours.
[
11
]
Proposed Changes to Rule 11892(b)(1)
FINRA proposes to amend Rule 11892(b)(1) to replace the phrase “Normal Market Hours” with “LULD Protected Hours,” to provide that “[i]f the execution time of the transaction(s) under review is during LULD Protected Hours, the transaction will not be reviewable as clearly erroneous . . .” This change would extend the LULD-based restrictions on clearly erroneous review currently in place during Normal Market Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours.
[
12
]
FINRA also proposes to amend Rule 11892(b)(1)(B)'s reference to “Percentage Parameter” to incorporate the Percentage Parameter that applies to Overnight Protected Hours. The amended provision would provide for the applicability of clearly erroneous review if the price of the transaction to buy (sell) that is the subject of the clearly erroneous review is greater than (less than) the Reference Price by an amount that equals or exceeds the applicable Percentage Parameter defined in Appendix A to the LULD Plan (with respect to the Price Bands that apply during Normal Market Hours) or the “Overnight Percentage Parameter” defined in Section VIII of the LULD Plan (with respect to Overnight Protected Hours).
In addition to these changes, FINRA also proposes to make a non-substantive change to Rule 11892(b)(1)(A), substituting the term “LULD Plan” for “the Plan to Address Extraordinary Market Volatility Pursuant to Rule 608 of Regulation NMS under the Act (the `Limit Up-Limit Down Plan' or `LULD Plan'),” as the “LULD Plan” would be defined in the proposed revision to Rule 11892(a)(1).
Proposed Changes to Rule 11892(b)(2) and (c)(3)
As noted above, current Rule 11892(b)(1)(A) permits clearly erroneous review even during Normal Market Hours when the transaction in question is in an NMS Stock that is not subject to the LULD Plan,
e.g.,
rights and warrants. Such transactions are reviewed as set out in Rule 11892(b)(2), including the Numerical Guidelines set out in the table accompanying Rule 11892(b)(2)(A). FINRA now proposes to introduce a similar provision regarding transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan that are executed during the Overnight Protected Hours; such transactions would be subject to the same Numerical Guidelines as transactions currently occurring outside Normal Market Hours.
The heading of Rule 11892(b)(2) addresses “[r]eview of transactions occurring outside of Normal Market Hours or eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (b)(1)(A).” FINRA proposes to replace “Normal Market Hours” with “LULD Protected Hours” to specify the timeframe of transactions not covered by LULD Price Bands. FINRA further proposes to replace the phrase “eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (b)(1)(A)” (which, in the current rule, means transactions executed during Normal Market Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan) with “during LULD Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan.” This proposed language would cover transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan during Normal Market Hours and expand the same treatment to transactions executed in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan during Overnight Protected Hours. As such, the proposed change is not novel.
FINRA proposes to make conforming changes throughout the rule—namely, in the text of paragraphs (b)(2)(A), (b)(2)(B), (b)(2)(C), and (c)(3).
[
13
]
In each case, FINRA proposes to replace the phrase “a transaction executed outside of Normal Market Hours or eligible for
(
printed page 75958)
review pursuant to paragraph (b)(1)(A) of this Rule” with “a transaction executed outside of LULD Protected Hours or during LULD Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan.”
FINRA also proposes to make corresponding changes to the headings of the table accompanying Rule 11892(b)(2)(A). FINRA proposes to change the heading of the second column from “Normal Market Hours Numerical Guidelines for Transactions Eligible for Review Pursuant to Paragraph (b)(1)(A)” to “Numerical Guidelines for Transactions Executed During Normal Market Hours in NMS Stocks Not Subject to the LULD Plan.” This change would replace “eligible for review pursuant to paragraph (b)(1)(A)” with the fuller description that such transactions are “executed during Normal Market Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan,” and is not a substantive change.
Similarly, FINRA proposes to change the heading of the third column from “Outside Normal Market Hours Numerical Guidelines” to “Numerical Guidelines for Transactions Executed Outside LULD Protected Hours or During Overnight Protected Hours in NMS Stocks Not Subject to the LULD Plan.” The proposed change addresses the fact that transactions executed during Overnight Protected Hours in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan are eligible for clearly erroneous review—just as are transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan executed during Normal Market Hours—using the Numerical Guidelines that currently apply outside of Normal Market Hours.
Together, these proposed changes would extend the eligibility of clearly erroneous review for transactions in NMS Stocks not subject to the LULD Plan that is currently in place during Normal Market Hours to the Overnight Protected Hours, and would apply the Commission's recent approval of Overnight Price Bands to the clearly erroneous executions rules.
FINRA has filed the proposed rule change for immediate effectiveness and has requested that the SEC waive the requirement that the proposed rule change not become operative for 30 days after the date of filing, so FINRA can implement the proposed rule change on December 6, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
FINRA believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 15A(b)(6) of the Act,
[
14
]
which requires, among other things, that FINRA rules be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
FINRA believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with just and equitable principles of trade because it extends the premise of the current rule—
i.e.,
that clearly erroneous review should be generally unavailable any time a transaction is executed within LULD Price Bands at a time when the Price Bands were available and correct. Currently, LULD Price Bands are available only during Normal Market Hours, meaning that the restrictions on clearly erroneous review described above apply only during Normal Market Hours. With the introduction of Overnight Price Bands, FINRA believes that extending such restrictions on clearly erroneous review to the period when Overnight Price Bands are in place would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by enhancing the transparency and consistency of the rule.
The resulting rule would thus extend the LULD-related limits on clearly erroneous review that are applicable in Normal Market Hours to the overnight period. The proposed change would also be consistent with the Commission's rationale in approving the substantively similar prior exchange rule because it would limit any potential discordance between the LULD mechanism and CEE review in the overnight trading session, providing greater certainty to market participants that trades executed within the Overnight Price Bands will stand and not be broken.
[
15
]
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
FINRA does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
[
16
]
Rather than impacting competition, the proposed rule change would extend the premise of the current rule that clearly erroneous review should be generally unavailable any time a transaction is executed within LULD Price Bands at a time the Price Bands were available and correct. FINRA understands that the national securities exchanges have filed or will file similar proposals, the substance of which is substantively similar to this proposal. Thus, the proposed rule change will help to ensure consistency across SROs without implicating any competitive issues.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
Written comments were neither solicited nor received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
FINRA has designated this rule filing as non-controversial under Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
17
]
of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
18
]
thereunder. Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
19
]
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
20
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
21
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. FINRA has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay to the extent necessary, so that the proposed rule change may become operative upon effectiveness to enable the proposed rule change to become operative on December 6, 2026, when exchanges will commence 23/5 Trading. Waiving the 30-day operative delay in this manner will help to ensure consistency across SROs and avoid confusion. For these reasons, and because the proposed rule change raises no new or novel legal or regulatory issues, the Commission finds that waiver of the operative delay is consistent with the protection of
(
printed page 75959)
investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change to be operative upon filing.
[
22
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
23
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-FINRA-2026-027 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-FINRA-2026-027. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of FINRA. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-FINRA-2026-027 and should be submitted on or before December 15, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
24
]

Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106947; File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-094]
November 20, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 10, 2026, Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BZX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The
(
printed page 75897)
Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (“BZX” or the “Exchange”) is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission” or “SEC”) a proposed rule change to amend the annual listing fees applicable to Outcome Strategy ETPs listed on the Exchange, which are set forth in BZX Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(iii), to (i) provide that Outcome Strategy ETPs with outcome periods that begin in different calendar years constitute separate series for purposes of the annual listing fee cap, and (ii) replace the single $16,000 annual listing fee cap with a two-tier cap of $16,000 for a series of four or fewer Outcome Strategy ETPs and $25,000 for a series of five or more Outcome Strategy ETPs. Changes to the fee schedule pursuant to this proposal are effective upon filing and will become operative on January 1, 2027. The text of the proposed rule change is attached as Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​bzx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
On August 30, 2011, the Exchange received approval of rules applicable to the qualification, listing and delisting of companies on the Exchange,
[
3
]
which it modified on February 8, 2012 in order to adopt pricing for the listing of exchange-traded products (“ETPs”)
[
4
]
on the Exchange.
[
5
]
On August 30, 2019, the Exchange adopted an annual listing fee cap for Outcome Strategy Series (the “2019 filing”),
[
6
]
and in January 2021 expanded criterion (iii) of the applicable rule to include ETPs based on two or more underlying instruments.
[
7
]
The Exchange now proposes to amend BZX Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(iii) to refine the manner in which the annual fee cap applies to Outcome Strategy ETPs.
Currently, Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(iii) provides: “Where an issuer lists multiple ETPs that are each designed to provide (i) a pre-defined set of returns; (ii) over a specified outcome period; (iii) based on the performance of the same underlying instruments; and (iv) each employ the same outcome strategy for achieving the pre-defined set of returns (each an “Outcome Strategy ETP”), the collective maximum annual listing fee applicable to such series of Outcome Strategy ETPs will be $16,000 per year.” In addition, Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E) provides that an issuer will be charged the lowest applicable fee among the categories set forth in Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(i) through (vi). Under Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(vi), an ETP that does not otherwise qualify for a lower fee is subject to an annual listing fee based on the consolidated average daily volume (“CADV”) of the ETP in the fourth quarter of the preceding calendar year, ranging from $5,000 to $7,000.
Outcome Strategy ETPs are designed to provide a particular set of returns over a specified outcome period based on the performance of an underlying instrument during that outcome period. As described in the 2019 filing, an Outcome Strategy ETP may employ a “Buffer Strategy” under which the ETP seeks to provide investment returns that match the gains of the reference asset(s) up to a Cap Level while guarding against certain declines in the same reference asset(s) through a Buffer Level over a defined Outcome Period, and the ETP resets at the end of the Outcome Period to employ the same strategy for the next Outcome Period. Because the applicable Outcome Period is central to the product design, issuers generally list Outcome Strategy ETPs in at least quarterly versions of the same strategy (a “Quarterly Series”) and may also list monthly versions, meaning that an issuer may list twelve ETPs that employ the same strategy but have different Outcome Periods (a “Monthly Series”). The 2019 filing explained that, under the existing $16,000 cap, a quarterly series would pay $4,000 per ETP and a monthly series would pay $1,333.33 per ETP. The Exchange also explained that each ETP in such a series uses the same reference instrument and strategy, has nearly identical holdings to the other ETPs in the series, and permits the Exchange to leverage the same surveillance and continued listing monitoring processes across the series.
The current rule does not specify any temporal boundary for a series, and as a result an issuer can continue adding Outcome Strategy ETPs with successive outcome periods to a single series indefinitely, including funds whose outcome periods begin years apart and whose cap levels and buffer levels were set under different market conditions. The Exchange therefore proposes to amend criterion (ii) to refer to ETPs designed to provide a pre-defined set of returns over a specified outcome period that begins in the same calendar year. As a result, Outcome Strategy ETPs with outcome periods beginning in different calendar years would constitute separate series for purposes of the annual listing fee cap. In applying the amended rule, the Exchange will include each Outcome Strategy ETP in the series for the calendar year in which its outcome period begins, and will determine the number of Outcome Strategy ETPs in a series as of the date the annual listing fee is assessed. For example, an Outcome Strategy ETP with an outcome period of January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027 and an Outcome Strategy ETP with an outcome period of January 1, 2028 through December 31, 2028 that otherwise satisfy criteria (i), (iii), and (iv) would be part of separate series, each subject to its own annual listing fee cap. Because each Outcome Strategy ETP is assigned to a series based solely on the year its outcome period begins, an ETP whose outcome period spans two calendar years is counted in only one series. For example, an Outcome Strategy ETP with an outcome period of July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028 would be part of the 2027 series only, and would not also be counted in the 2028 series.
The Exchange believes this calendar-year delineation is principled and administrable. First, Rule 14.13(b)(2)(K) provides that, unless otherwise specified, the Exchange assesses annual fees upon initial listing and in the first
(
printed page 75898)
quarter of the calendar year.
[
8
]
A calendar-year series therefore aligns the series concept with the period in which annual fees are assessed. Second, issuers typically launch, name, and market Outcome Strategy ETPs by the month and year of the applicable outcome period, and key terms such as cap levels are set at the beginning of that period based on then-current market conditions, so ETPs whose outcome periods begin in the same year share a common launch cycle. Third, the calendar year is an objective, uniform, and administrable standard that requires no subjective judgment by the Exchange. Finally, this approach preserves the original purpose of the fee cap, which was to accommodate the quarterly or monthly versions of a strategy that an issuer lists within an annual cycle, while preventing a single cap from covering an unbounded number of products over multiple years.
The Exchange also proposes to replace the current single $16,000 annual listing fee cap with a two-tier cap of $16,000 for a series of four or fewer Outcome Strategy ETPs and $25,000 for a series of five or more Outcome Strategy ETPs. The four-ETP threshold corresponds to the Quarterly Series described in the 2019 filing, and the second tier applies to series with more frequent issuance, such as a Monthly Series. Consistent with the approach in the 2019 filing, the following describes the annual listing fees that each type of series pays today, the fees each would pay under the proposal, and the fees each would pay absent the cap, assuming each ETP would otherwise be subject to a CADV-based annual listing fee of between $5,000 and $7,000 under Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(vi).
Quarterly Series.
Today, a Quarterly Series of four Outcome Strategy ETPs pays the $16,000 cap, or $4,000 per ETP. Under the proposal, a Quarterly Series would continue to pay $16,000, or $4,000 per ETP, so the proposal does not change the annual listing fees paid by a Quarterly Series. Absent the cap, the four ETPs would pay between $20,000 and $28,000 in the aggregate ($5,000 to $7,000 per ETP). Accordingly, both today and under the proposal, a Quarterly Series receives a reduction of between $4,000 and $12,000 in the aggregate, or between $1,000 and $3,000 per ETP (approximately 20% to 43%).
Monthly Series.
Today, a Monthly Series of twelve Outcome Strategy ETPs also pays the $16,000 cap, or approximately $1,333.33 per ETP, the same aggregate amount paid by a Quarterly Series with one-third as many ETPs. Under the proposal, a Monthly Series would pay the $25,000 cap, or approximately $2,083.33 per ETP, an increase of $9,000 in the aggregate, or $750 per ETP. Absent the cap, the twelve ETPs would pay between $60,000 and $84,000 in the aggregate. Accordingly, under the proposal a Monthly Series would continue to receive a reduction of between $35,000 and $59,000 in the aggregate, or between approximately $2,916.67 and $4,916.67 per ETP (approximately 58% to 70%), as compared to a current reduction of between $44,000 and $68,000 (approximately 73% to 81%).
Under the current single cap, the effective per-ETP fee for a Monthly Series is one-third of that paid by a Quarterly Series, and an issuer may add eight additional ETPs to a Quarterly Series without any increase in annual listing fees. The proposal narrows, but does not eliminate, that difference. Under the proposal, a Monthly Series would continue to pay a lower effective fee per ETP than a Quarterly Series (approximately $2,083.33 as compared to $4,000, or approximately 48% less) and would continue to receive a larger percentage reduction relative to the CADV-based fees than a Quarterly Series. Series of between five and eleven ETPs would likewise pay $25,000, or between $5,000 and approximately $2,272.73 per ETP, which in each case is no more than the lowest CADV-based annual listing fee. Because an issuer is charged the lowest applicable fee, no series will pay more than the aggregate annual fees that its constituent ETPs would otherwise pay under Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E).
The Exchange will implement the proposed change beginning with annual listing fees assessed for calendar year 2027. As noted above, unless otherwise specified, the Exchange assesses annual fees upon initial listing and in the first quarter of the calendar year.
[
9
]
Accordingly, the proposal will have no effect on annual listing fees already assessed for calendar year 2026, and this filing will provide issuers with notice of the change before the assessment of annual listing fees for calendar year 2027.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the objectives of Section 6 of the Act,
[
10
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and 6(b)(5),
[
11
]
in particular, as it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among its issuers, and it does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposal is reasonable because the use of the calendar year in which an outcome period begins aligns the operation of the fee cap with the Exchange's annual fee cycle and with the manner in which issuers launch and market Outcome Strategy ETPs. The proposal also retains a substantial discount relative to per-ETP fees for both types of series described in the 2019 filing. A Quarterly Series would continue to pay $16,000, or $4,000 per ETP, the same amount it pays today and the same result described in the 2019 filing. A Monthly Series would pay $25,000, or approximately $2,083.33 per ETP, which remains between approximately 58% and 70% below the aggregate CADV-based fees that would otherwise apply, and remains well below the lowest CADV-based annual listing fee of $5,000 per ETP. Any series of five or more ETPs would pay no more than $5,000 per ETP, and the effective fee per ETP declines further as the series grows.
The Exchange believes that the proposal provides for an equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges because it will apply equally to all issuers and to all Outcome Strategy Series meeting the objective criteria in Rule 14.13(b)(2)(E)(iii). The proposal allocates fees in relation to the number of Outcome Strategy ETPs an issuer lists in a given year, and issuers that list more products in a calendar year would bear a modestly larger share of the applicable annual listing fees while continuing to receive a lower effective fee per ETP.
The Exchange believes that the proposal is not unfairly discriminatory because it relies on objective criteria, namely the calendar year in which an Outcome Strategy ETP's outcome period begins and the number of ETPs in the relevant series, and those criteria would apply in the same manner to every issuer. Quarterly Series and Monthly Series are not similarly situated: a Monthly Series consists of three times as many listed ETPs as a Quarterly Series, and under the current single cap pays the same aggregate fee as a Quarterly Series, resulting in an effective per-ETP fee that is one-third of the per-ETP fee paid by a Quarterly Series. The proposal does not reverse that relationship. A Monthly Series would continue to pay a lower effective fee per ETP than a Quarterly Series and
(
printed page 75899)
would continue to receive a larger discount relative to the CADV-based fees. Accordingly, the proposal does not provide a Quarterly Series with any benefit it does not receive today, and any remaining difference in the per-ETP fees paid by Quarterly and Monthly Series favors the Monthly Series and reflects only the number of ETPs the issuer has elected to list. Further, both tiers are available to every issuer, and any issuer may elect to list a Quarterly Series, a Monthly Series, or a series of any other frequency. The proposal also continues to recognize, consistent with the 2019 filing, that Outcome Strategy ETPs by their nature require multiple listings and that listing fees should not be the reason additional outcome periods are unavailable to investors. Distinguishing series by the calendar year in which an outcome period begins is a neutral line tied to the period in which annual fees are assessed, not to any particular issuer.
Furthermore, the marketplace for ETP listings is extremely competitive and there are several other national securities exchanges that offer ETP listings. Transfers between listing venues occur frequently for numerous reasons, including listing fees. Issuers of Outcome Strategy ETPs may transfer their listings to another venue if they deem the Exchange's listing fees excessive. The proposed rule change reflects a competitive pricing structure, which the Exchange believes will enhance competition both among ETP issuers and among listing venues, to the benefit of investors.
Based on the foregoing, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will burden intramarket competition because the amendments to the annual listing fee cap for Outcome Strategy ETPs will apply uniformly to all issuers of Outcome Strategy ETPs based on objective criteria, namely the calendar year in which an outcome period begins and the number of ETPs in a series. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will burden intermarket competition because the market for ETP listings is highly competitive, and issuers may transfer the listing of an ETP to another national securities exchange if they deem the Exchange's listing fees excessive. The proposed rule change is a competitive pricing decision that reflects the Exchange's determination to tailor the annual listing fee cap for Outcome Strategy ETPs in a manner that better aligns with the Exchange's annual fee structure and the number of products listed in a series.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
12
]
and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4
[
13
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-094 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-094. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeBZX-2026-094 and should be submitted on or before December 15, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
14
]

Secretary.

SUMMARY:
Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) and its implementing regulations, FRA seeks approval of the Information Collection Request (ICR) summarized below. https://www.regulations.gov

FRA will summarize comments received in response to this notice in a subsequent notice, made available to the public, and include them in its information collection submission to OMB for approval.

Title:
Emergency Escape Breathing Apparatus (EEBA) Standards.
OMB Control Number:
2130-0620.
Abstract:
In 2024, FRA issued a final rule,
[
1
]
amending subpart C of
49 CFR part 227
requiring any freight railroad to provide a covered employee with an appropriate atmosphere-supplying EEBA when occupying a locomotive cab of a train transporting a poison inhalation hazard (PIH) material that, if released due to a railroad accident/incident, would pose an inhalation hazard to the occupants. In particular, subpart C is intended to protect these employees from the risk of exposure to PIH material while they are located in, or during escape from, the locomotive cab.
Railroads transporting PIH materials on the general railroad system are required to establish EEBA programs covering selection, procurement, provision, inspection, maintenance, replacement, and employee instruction. Railroads must identify participating employees or positions to ensure adequate supply and proper training, and store EEBAs in locomotive cabs for quick access during hazardous inhalation releases.
FRA will use the information collected to ensure freight railroads establish and implement EEBA programs to improve the safety of covered employees, and to confirm compliance with the regulation.
In this 60-day notice, FRA has made multiple adjustments to the previously approved burden hours. FRA's adjustments have decreased the previously approved burden from 1,670 hours to 1,232 hours.
Overall, the reduction in burden hours stems from updated estimates indicating that all railroads have established comprehensive written EEBA plans in compliance with § 227.217. Further, FRA projects that only three new railroads will commence operations during this three-year information collection cycle.

Title:
Positive Train Control and Other Signal Systems.
OMB Control Number:
2130-0553.
Abstract:
Since December 31, 2020, by law, positive train control (PTC) systems have generally governed rail operations on PTC-mandated main lines, which encompass approximately 59,000 route miles. Railroads continue to file and update the governing FRA-approved plans, including PTC Implementation Plans, PTC Development Plans, and PTC Safety Plans. The statutory mandate requires railroads to submit to FRA Quarterly Reports on PTC System Performance on Form FRA F 6180.152, under
49 U.S.C. 20157(m)
. Such reporting enables FRA to oversee the failure rate and reliability of PTC technology.
In addition, among other reporting requirements, FRA's regulations require that both railroads and PTC vendors and suppliers notify FRA of certain PTC system errors and malfunctions.
49 CFR 236.1023
. For example, railroads must maintain a database of all safety-relevant hazards identified in their PTC Safety Plans (PTCSP) and those that had not previously been identified in their PTCSPs.
49 CFR 236.1023(e)
. If the frequency of a safety-relevant hazard exceeds the thresholds in a railroad's PTCSP, or such hazard has not been previously identified in a railroad's risk analysis, then the railroad must notify FRA of the failure, malfunction, or defective condition that decreased or eliminated the safety functionality of the railroad's PTC system.
49 CFR 236.1023(e)(1)
. In addition, FRA's regulations require PTC vendors and suppliers to notify FRA of any safety-relevant failure, defective condition, or previously unidentified hazard discovered by the vendor or supplier and the identity of each affected and notified railroad.
In this 60-day notice, FRA has made multiple adjustments to the previously approved burden hours. While some reported burdens have decreased, the overall burden hours increased from the previously approved 51,931 hours to 53,174 hours.
FRA identified burden hours that have previously been reported for public comments. The submission of public comments in response to a
Federal Register
notice falls outside the PRA's definition of information under
5 CFR 1320.3(h)(4)
. Consequently, FRA is removing the burden previously attributed to public comments under §§ 236.913, 236.1011, and 236.1021.
Further, FRA has determined that requirements under § 236.1001, which permits railroads to prescribe more stringent internal rules, and § 236.1017 regarding independent third-party assessments, also fall outside the PRA's definition of information under
5 CFR 1320.3(h)
. The previously reported burden hours for these sections have been removed.
In addition, the deadlines for certain Class II and III railroads to submit progress reports to FRA concerning the installation of onboard PTC apparatuses have expired. Accordingly, the burden hours previously associated with § 236.1006(b) have been removed from this submission.
Finally, FRA has updated the burden estimate for § 236.587, which requires the retention of departure test records for at least 92 days. This revised estimate is the primary driver for the net increase of 1,243 annual burden hours. FRA calculated this update using data reported by railroads, ensuring the estimate provides a more precise reflection of the actual administrative burden associated with this regulatory requirement.

AGENCY:
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
ACTION:
Notice with comment period.
SUMMARY:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), as part of its continuing effort to reduce public burden and maximize the utility of government information, invites the general public and other federal agencies the opportunity to comment on a continuing information collection, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. This notice invites comment on an information collection project titled Pulmonary Function Testing Course Approval Program. The program consists of an application submitted by potential sponsors (universities, hospitals, and private consulting firms) who seek NIOSH approval to conduct courses, and if approved, notification to NIOSH of any course or faculty changes during the approval period, which is limited to five years.
DATES:
CDC must receive written comments on or before January 25, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments, identified by Docket No. CDC-2026-1816 by either of the following methods:
Federal eRulemaking Portal:
www.regulations.gov
.
Follow the instructions for submitting comments.
Mail:
Jeffrey M. Zirger, Information Collection Review Office, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 1600 Clifton Road NE, MS H21-8, Atlanta, Georgia 30329.
Instructions:
All submissions received must include the agency name and Docket Number. CDC will post, without change, all relevant comments to
www.regulations.gov
.
Please note:
Submit all comments through the Federal eRulemaking portal (
www.regulations.gov
) or by U.S. mail to the address listed above.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
To request more information on the proposed project or to obtain a copy of the information collection plan and instruments, contact Jeffrey M. Zirger, Information Collection Review Office, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 1600 Clifton Road NE, MS H21-8, Atlanta, Georgia 30329; Telephone: 404-639-7570; Email:
omb@cdc.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA) (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3520
), federal agencies must obtain approval from the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for each collection of information they conduct or sponsor. In addition, the PRA also requires federal agencies to provide a 60-day notice in the
Federal Register
concerning each proposed collection of information, including each new proposed collection, each proposed extension of existing collection of information, and each reinstatement of previously approved information collection before submitting the collection to the OMB for approval. To comply with this requirement, we are publishing this notice of a proposed data collection as described below.
The OMB is particularly interested in comments that will help:
1. Evaluate whether the proposed collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information will have practical utility;
2. Evaluate the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the proposed collection of information, including the validity of the methodology and assumptions used;
3. Enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected;
4. Minimize the burden of the collection of information on those who are to respond, including through the use of appropriate automated, electronic, mechanical, or other technological collection techniques or other forms of information technology,
e.g.,
permitting electronic submissions of responses; and
5. Assess information collection costs.
Proposed Project
Pulmonary Function Testing Course Approval Program. (OMB Control No. 0920-0138, Exp. 4/30/2026)—Extension—National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).
Background and Brief Description
NIOSH has the responsibility under the Occupational Safety and Health Administration's Cotton Dust Standard,
29 CFR 1920.1043
, for approving courses to train technicians to perform pulmonary function testing in the cotton industry. Successful completion of a NIOSH-approved course is mandatory under this Standard. In addition, regulations at
42 CFR 37.95(a)
specify that persons administering spirometry tests for the national Coal Workers' Health Surveillance Program must successfully complete a NIOSH-approved spirometry training course and maintain a valid certificate by periodically completing NIOSH-approved spirometry refresher training courses. Also,
29 CFR 1910.1053(i)(2)(iv)
,
29 CFR 1910.1053(i)(3)
,
29 CFR 1926.1153(h)(2)(iv)
and
29 CFR 1926.1153(h)(3)
specify that pulmonary function tests for initial and periodic examinations in general industry and construction performed under the Respirable Crystalline Silica Standard should be administered by a spirometry technician with a current certificate from a NIOSH-approved spirometry course.
To carry out its responsibility, NIOSH maintains a Pulmonary Function Testing Course Approval Program. The program consists of an application submitted by potential sponsors (universities, hospitals, and private consulting firms) who seek NIOSH approval to conduct courses, and if approved, notification to NIOSH of any course or faculty changes during the approval period, which is limited to five years. The application form and added materials, including an agenda, curriculum vitae, and course materials are reviewed by NIOSH to determine if the applicant has developed a program which adheres to the criteria required in the Standard. Following approval, any subsequent changes to the course are submitted by course sponsors via letter or email and reviewed by NIOSH staff
(
printed page 75859)
to assure that the changes in faculty or course content continue to meet course requirements. Course sponsors also voluntarily submit an annual report to inform NIOSH of their course activity level and any faculty changes. Sponsors who elect to have their approval renewed for an additional five-year period submit a renewal application and supporting documentation for review by NIOSH staff to ensure the course curriculum meets all current standard requirements. Approved courses that elect to offer NIOSH-Approved Spirometry Refresher Courses must submit a separate application and supporting documents for review by NIOSH staff. Institutions and organizations throughout the country voluntarily submit applications and materials to become approved course sponsors and administer training. Submissions are required for NIOSH to evaluate a course and determine whether it meets the criteria in the Standard and whether technicians will be adequately trained as mandated under the Standard.
CDC requests OMB approval for a total of 144 estimated annual burden hours. There is no cost to respondents other than their time.

The Marine Corps Marathon Organization (MCMO) is tasked with the management of the Marine Corps Marathon (MCM) races on behalf of the Marine Corps. I. Introduction
Pursuant to
39 CFR 3041.405
, the Commission gives notice that the Postal Service filed request(s) for the Commission to consider matters related to Competitive negotiated service agreement(s). The request(s) may propose the addition of a negotiated service agreement from the Competitive product list or the modification of an existing product currently appearing on the Competitive product list.
The public portions of the Postal Service's request(s) can be accessed via the Commission's website (
http://www.prc.gov
). Non-public portions of the Postal Service's request(s), if any, can be accessed through compliance with the requirements of
39 CFR 3011.301
.
[
1
]
Section II identifies the docket number(s) associated with each Postal Service request, if any, that will be reviewed in a public proceeding as defined by
39 CFR 3010.101(p)
, the title of each such request, the request's acceptance date, and the authority cited by the Postal Service for each request. For each such request, the Commission appoints an officer of the Commission to represent the interests of the general public in the proceeding, pursuant to
39 U.S.C. 505
and
39 CFR 3000.114
(Public Representative). The Public Representative does not represent any individual person, entity or particular point of view, and, when Commission attorneys are appointed, no attorney-client relationship is established. Section II also establishes comment deadline(s) pertaining to each such request.
The Commission invites comments on whether the Postal Service's request(s) identified in Section II, if any, are consistent with the policies of title 39. Applicable statutory and regulatory requirements include
39 U.S.C. 3632
,
39 U.S.C. 3633
,
39 U.S.C. 3642
,
39 CFR part 3035
, and
39 CFR part 3041
. Comment deadline(s) for each such request, if any, appear in Section II.
Section III identifies the docket number(s) associated with each Postal Service request, if any, to add a standardized distinct product to the Competitive product list or to amend a standardized distinct product, the title of each such request, the request's acceptance date, and the authority cited by the Postal Service for each request. Standardized distinct products are negotiated service agreements that are variations of one or more Competitive products, and for which financial models, minimum rates, and classification criteria have undergone advance Commission review.
See
39 CFR 3041.110(n)
;
39 CFR 3041.205(a)
. Such requests are reviewed in summary proceedings pursuant to
39 CFR 3041.325(c)(2)
and
39 CFR 3041.505(f)(1)
. Pursuant to
39 CFR 3041.405(c)-(d)
, the Commission does not appoint a Public Representative or request public comment in proceedings to review such requests.

title: Wireless Telecommunications Bureau Seeks Comment on Whether Proposed Upper C-Band Relocation Coordinator Satisfies Selection Criteria
abstract: In this document, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) invites interested parties to comment on whether the proposed Relocation Coordinator selected by the eligible space station operators in the Upper C-band satisfies the criteria established by the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) in Upper C-band (3.98-4.2 GHz); Expanding Flexible Use of the 3.7 to 4.2 GHz Band, GN Docket Nos. 25-59 and 18-122, Report and Order, Order of Proposed Modification, and Order on Reconsideration, FCC 26-46 (July 24, 2026) (Upper C-band R&O). In the Upper C-band R&O, the Commission adopted rules to make 160 megahertz of mid-band spectrum available for flexible use throughout the contiguous United States by transitioning incumbent Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) operations out of 4.0-4.16 GHz. The Upper C-band R&O required eligible space station operators to select a Relocation Coordinator that will be responsible for managing the overall transition and coordinating relocation actions among eligible FSS space station operators, incumbent FSS earth station operators, and new Upper C-band flexible use licensees.
dates: Comments are due on or before December 3, 2026; reply comments are due on or before December 14, 2026.

ex parte
presentations and memoranda summarizing oral
ex parte
presentations, and all attachments thereto, must be filed through the electronic comment filing system available for that proceeding, and must be filed in their native format (

.doc, .xml, .ppt, searchable .pdf). Participants in this proceeding should familiarize themselves with the Commission's
ex parte
rules.
Synopsis
With this Public Notice, the Wireless Telecommunications Bureau (Bureau) seeks comment on whether the proposed Relocation Coordinator selected by the eligible space station operators in the Upper C-band satisfies the criteria established by the Commission in the
Upper C-band R&O.
On July 24, 2026, the Commission released the
Upper C-band R&O,
which adopted rules to make 160 megahertz of mid-band spectrum available for flexible use throughout the contiguous United States by transitioning incumbent Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) operations out of 4.0-4.16 GHz.
The
Upper C-band R&O
required eligible Fixed Satellite Service (FSS) space station operators to select, no later than January 1, 2027, a Relocation Coordinator that will be responsible for managing the overall transition and coordinating relocation actions among eligible FSS space station operators, incumbent FSS earth station operators, and new Upper C-band flexible use licensees. The
Upper C-band R&O
required that the Relocation Coordinator “must be able to demonstrate that it has
(
printed page 75857)
the requisite expertise to perform the duties required in this context, which broadly include: (1) coordinating the schedule for clearing the band; (2) performing engineering analysis, as necessary, to determine necessary earth station migration actions; (3) assigning obligations, as necessary, for earth station migrations; (4) coordinating with the Upper C-band licensees throughout the transition process; (5) assessing and tracking the completion of the transition in each PEA and determining the Upper C-band wireless licensees' ability to commence operations; and (6) mediating scheduling disputes.”
On November 17, 2026, all three eligible space station operators announced that they had selected RSM US LLP (RSM) to serve as the Relocation Coordinator. We seek comment on whether RSM satisfies the selection criteria established by the Commission in the
Upper C-band R&O.
As directed by the Commission in the
Upper C-band R&O,
following the comment period, the Bureau will issue a final order determining whether the selection criteria have been satisfied. In the event the selection criteria are not met, the selection committee will restart its evaluation process and identify a new proposed entity that will be subject to the same public comment and review process by the Bureau.

Needs and Uses:
The primary purpose of the Navy Family Accountability and Assessment System (NFAAS) is personnel accountability following a natural or man-made disaster for all Active Duty, Reserve, Navy Civilians, Contractors serving Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS), and their dependents. NFAAS also assesses the impact of the disaster on Navy families and Command's ability to fulfill its missions by providing services and tracking support provided to families in recovery. Additionally, NFAAS supports the sponsor and family members during Sailor Individual Augmentation deployments. This collection of information is authorized by Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 3001.02, “Personnel Accountability in Conjunction with Natural or Manmade Disasters,” and Office of the Chief of Naval Operations Instruction (OPNAVINST) 3006.1, “Personnel Accountability in Conjunction with Catastrophic Events.” Respondents include all Navy personnel who are responsible for accounting after a disaster and updating or verifying sponsor and dependent information. Per DoDI 3001.02, this includes all active and reserve military personnel, Navy civilian employees, Nonappropriated Fund employees, Navy Exchange employees, and OCONUS contractors. Continental United States (CONUS) contractors are not included. To comply with the Paperwork Reduction Act, the burden estimates in this information collection request only account for respondents who are members of the public.
