SUMMARY:
This amendment adopts miscellaneous amendments to the required IFR (instrument flight rules) altitudes and changeover points for certain Federal airways, jet routes, or direct routes for which a minimum or maximum en-route authorized IFR altitude is prescribed. This regulatory action is needed because of changes occurring in the National Airspace System. These changes are designed to provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace under instrument conditions in the affected areas.
DATES:
Effective 0901 UTC, December 24, 2026.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Brian Murphy, Manager, Aeronautical Information Services, Aeronautical Information Group, Aeronautical Data Team, Federal Aviation Administration. Mailing Address: FAA Headquarters, Aeronautical Information Group, 800 Independence Ave. SW, Bldg. 10A, Room 507L, Washington, DC 20591. Telephone (202) 267-4389.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
This amendment to part 95 of the Federal Aviation Regulations (
14 CFR part 95
) amends, suspends, or revokes IFR altitudes governing the operation of all aircraft in flight over a specified route or any portion of that route, as well as the changeover points (COPs) for Federal airways, jet routes, or direct routes as prescribed in part 95.
The Rule
The specified IFR altitudes, when used in conjunction with the prescribed
(
printed page 75767)
changeover points for those routes, ensure navigation aid coverage that is adequate for safe flight operations and free of frequency interference. The reasons and circumstances that create the need for this amendment involve matters of flight safety and operational efficiency in the National Airspace System, are related to published aeronautical charts that are essential to the user and provide for the safe and efficient use of the navigable airspace. In addition, those various reasons or circumstances require making this amendment effective before the next scheduled charting and publication date of the flight information to assure its timely availability to the user. The effective date of this amendment reflects those considerations. In view of the close and immediate relationship between these regulatory changes and safety in air commerce, I find that notice and public procedure before adopting this amendment are impracticable and contrary to the public interest and that good cause exists for making the amendment effective in less than 30 days.
Conclusion
The FAA has determined that this regulation only involves an established body of technical regulations for which frequent and routine amendments are necessary to keep them operationally current. It, therefore—(1) is not a “significant regulatory action” under
Executive Order 12866
; (2) is not a “significant rule” under DOT Regulatory Policies and Procedures (
44 FR 11034
; February 26, 1979); and (3) does not warrant preparation of a regulatory evaluation as the anticipated impact is so minimal. For the same reason, the FAA certifies that this amendment will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the criteria of the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

AGENCY:
Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
This document provides the public notice that CSX Transportation Inc. (CSXT) petitioned FRA for relief from certain regulations concerning tests and inspections of extended haul trains.
DATES:
FRA must receive comments on the petition by January 25, 2027. FRA will consider comments received after that date to the extent practicable.
ADDRESSES:
Comments:
Comments related to this docket may be submitted by going to
https://www.regulations.gov
and following the online instructions for submitting comments.
(
printed page 75970)
Instructions:
All submissions must include the agency name and docket number. All comments received will be posted without change to
https://www.regulations.gov
;
this includes any personal information. Please see the Privacy Act heading in the
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
section of this document for Privacy Act information related to any submitted comments or materials.
Docket:
For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and follow the online instructions for accessing the docket.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Michael Barron, Railroad Safety Specialist, FRA Motive Power & Equipment Division, telephone: 202-493-1367, email:
michael.barron@dot.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Under
part 211 of title 49 Code of Federal Regulations
(CFR), this document provides the public notice that by letter dated October 13, 2026, CSXT petitioned FRA for a waiver of compliance from certain provisions of the Federal railroad safety regulations contained at
49 CFR part 232
(Brake System Safety Standards for Freight and Other Non-Passenger Trains and Equipment; End-of-Train Devices). FRA assigned the petition Docket Number FRA-2026-2839.
Specifically, CSXT seeks relief from the requirements of § 232.207,
Class IA brake tests—1,000-mile inspection,
to permit 5 trains to operate over distances greater than 1,000 miles without a Class IA brake test. For these trains, CSX proposes a maximum operating distance of 1,500 miles, “consistent with the outer mileage limit and safety framework established for extended-haul trains in
49 CFR 232.213
.”
In support of its request, CSXT states that the subject trains will receive a Class I brake test (per § 232.205,
Class I brake test-initial terminal inspection
) and a freight car safety inspection (per part 215, Railroad Freight Car Safety Standards) at their initial terminals. Further, CSXT notes that the trains will also depart with 100 percent effective and operative brakes, except as permitted by FRA regulations, and will be subject to compliant en-route inspections following train makeup changes.
A copy of the petition, as well as any written communications concerning the petition, is available for review online at
www.regulations.gov
.
Interested parties are invited to participate in these proceedings by submitting written views, data, or comments. FRA does not anticipate scheduling a public hearing in connection with these proceedings since the facts do not appear to warrant a hearing. If any interested party desires an opportunity for oral comment and a public hearing, they should notify FRA, in writing, before the end of the comment period and specify the basis for their request.
Communications received by January 25, 2027 will be considered by FRA before final action is taken. Comments received after that date will be considered if practicable.
Privacy Act
Anyone can search the electronic form of any written communications and comments received into any of FRA's dockets by the name of the individual submitting the comment (or signing the document, if submitted on behalf of an association, business, labor union, etc.). Under
5 U.S.C. 553(c)
, DOT solicits comments from the public to inform its processes. DOT posts these comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to
www.regulations.gov
,
as described in the system of records notice (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS), which can be reviewed at
https://www.transportation.gov/​privacy
.
See also
https://www.regulations.gov/​privacy-notice
for the privacy notice of
regulations.gov.
Issued in Washington, DC.
John Karl Alexy,
Associate Administrator for Railroad Safety, Chief Safety Officer.

AGENCY:
Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), Department of Transportation (DOT).
ACTION:
Notice.
SUMMARY:
This document provides the public notice that the American Short Line and Regional Railroad Association (ASLRRA) petitioned FRA to extend an existing waiver of certain regulations related to hours of service.
DATES:
FRA must receive comments on the petition by January 25, 2027. FRA will consider comments received after that date to the extent practicable.
ADDRESSES:
Comments:
Comments related to this docket may be submitted by going to
https://www.regulations.gov
and following the online instructions for submitting comments.
Instructions:
All submissions must include the agency name and docket number. All comments received will be posted without change to
https://www.regulations.gov
;
this includes any personal information. Please see the Privacy Act heading in the
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION
section of this document for Privacy Act information related to any submitted comments or materials.
Docket:
For access to the docket to read background documents or comments received, go to
https://www.regulations.gov
and follow the online instructions for accessing the docket.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
William Smith, Railroad Safety Specialist, FRA Operating Practices Division, telephone: 682-305-6709, email:
William.Smith@dot.gov
.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Under
part 211 of title 49 Code of Federal Regulations
(CFR), this document provides the public notice that by letter dated October 8, 2026, ASLRRA petitioned FRA for an extension of a waiver of compliance from certain provisions of the Federal hours of service (HOS) laws contained at
49 U.S.C. 21103(a)(4)
. The relevant Docket Number is FRA-2009-0078.
Specifically, ASLRRA seeks to extend its existing waiver and states that “the waiver has been a success by all measures.” Further, ASLRRA notes that it is “not aware of a single reportable incident . . . attributable to fatigue during the effective period of the waiver on any participating railroad.” In addition, the petition notes that the waiver “has been essential to keeping short line railroads competitive, allowing for flexibility in operations.”
A copy of the petition, as well as any written communications concerning the petition, is available for review online at
www.regulations.gov
.
Interested parties are invited to participate in these proceedings by submitting written views, data, or comments. FRA does not anticipate scheduling a public hearing in connection with these proceedings since the facts do not appear to warrant a hearing. If any interested party desires an opportunity for oral comment and a public hearing, they should notify FRA, in writing, before the end of the comment period and specify the basis for their request.
Communications received by January 25, 2027 will be considered by FRA before final action is taken. Comments received after that date will be considered if practicable.
Privacy Act
Anyone can search the electronic form of any written communications and comments received into any of FRA's dockets by the name of the individual submitting the comment (or signing the document, if submitted on behalf of an association, business, labor union, etc.). Under
5 U.S.C. 553(c)
, DOT solicits comments from the public to inform its processes. DOT posts these comments, without edit, including any personal information the commenter provides, to
www.regulations.gov
,
as described in the system of records notice (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS), which can be reviewed at
https://www.transportation.gov/​privacy
.
See also
https://www.regulations.gov/​privacy-notice
for the privacy notice of
regulations.gov.
Issued in Washington, DC.
John Karl Alexy,
Associate Administrator for Railroad Safety, Chief Safety Officer.

Under
part 211 of title 49 Code of Federal Regulations
(CFR), this document provides the public notice that by letter dated October 19, 2026, BNSF petitioned FRA for a waiver of compliance from certain provisions of the Federal railroad safety regulations contained at
49 CFR part 232
(Brake System Safety Standards for Freight and Other Non-Passenger Trains and Equipment; End-of-Train Devices). FRA assigned the petition Docket Number FRA-2006-24812.
Specifically, BNSF seeks relief from the requirements of § 232.213,
Extended haul trains,
to continue operating certain extended haul trains up to a maximum of 1,702 miles. In support of its request, BNSF states that “trains operating under the waiver consistently generate fewer detector alerts than trains not operating under the waiver.” BNSF adds that “the ratio of equipment-caused train accidents per one million train miles has decreased in each year of the renewal term, and [now] sits at 0.158, substantially lower than any other U.S.-based Class I railroad.”

Department of Energy

[Docket No. CP26-572-000]
On August 31, 2026, Southern Star Central Gas Pipeline, Inc. (Southern Star) filed an application in Docket No. CP26-572 requesting a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity pursuant to Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act to construct and operate certain natural gas pipeline facilities. The proposed project is known as the Evergy McNew Power Plant Delivery Project (Project), which would provide up to 123,000 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d) of firm natural gas transportation service from Southern Star's existing mainline facilities to support operation of Evergy Kansas Central, Inc.'s planned new McNew Power Plant in Reno County, Kansas, a natural gas-fueled combined-cycle turbine generating facility that Southern Star asserts would enhance electric system reliability across the region.
[
1
]
On September 15, 2026, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission or FERC) issued its Notice of Application for the Project. Among other things, that notice alerted agencies issuing federal authorizations of the requirement to complete all necessary reviews and to reach a final decision on a request for a federal authorization within 90 days of the date of issuance of the Commission staff's environmental document for the Project.
This notice identifies Commission staff's intention to prepare an environmental assessment (EA) for the Project and the planned schedule for the completion of the environmental review.
[
2
]
The EA will be issued for a 30-day comment period.
Schedule for Environmental Review
Issuance of EA—June 7, 2027
90-day Federal Authorization Decision Deadline
[
3
]
—September 5, 2027
If a schedule change becomes necessary, additional notice will be provided so that the relevant agencies are kept informed of the Project's progress.
Project Description
The Evergy McNew Power Plant Delivery Project would consist of the following facilities, all within the state of Kansas:
Construction and operation of:
a new 1.6-mile-long 30-inch-diameter natural gas pipeline (Line RE) extending from a new, greenfield compressor station (Hutchinson Compressor Station) to the new Evergy Meter Station at the McNew Power Plant in Reno County;
the new Hutchinson Compressor Station and associated infrastructure along Southern Star's existing 26-inch-diameter Hugoton Loop Line RA in Reno County;
a new measurement and flow control station (Evergy Meter Station) and associated infrastructure at the McNew Plant in Reno County;
Modifications within the existing Hesston Compressor Station in Harvey County and the existing Stafford Compressor Station in Stafford County;
Installation of:
tie-in piping, a pig launcher, and associated infrastructure at the
(
printed page 75851)
connection to the existing Southern Star mainline system in Reno County; and
a new pig receiver and associated infrastructure at the Evergy Meter Station in Reno County.
Background
On October 1, 2026, the Commission issued a
Notice of Scoping Period Requesting Comments on Environmental Issues for the Proposed Evergy McNew Power Plant Delivery Project
(Notice of Scoping). The Notice of Scoping was sent to affected landowners; federal, state, and local government agencies; elected officials; environmental and public interest groups; Native American tribes; other interested parties; and local libraries and newspapers. In response to the Notice of Scoping, the Commission received comments from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District; and local residents Jared and Yolanda Oatney (comments filed by their counsel Diana Stanley on their behalf), and Alexia S. Welch. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers noted that should the Project involved dredge or fill in any waters of the United States, a Department of Army permit may be required. The Oatneys raised concerns on routing, geology, impacts on the nearby airfield, special status species, designated critical habitat, and general wildlife. Alexia Welch raised concerns on potential effects on groundwater resources; geology and geologic hazards; air quality and noise; emergency response capacity; routing and land use considerations; special status species; and the cumulative environmental impacts of existing and planned industrial development. All substantive comments will be addressed in the EA.
Additional Information
In order to receive notification of the issuance of the EA and to keep track of formal issuances and submittals in specific dockets, the Commission offers a free service called eSubscription. This service provides automatic notification of filings made to subscribed dockets, document summaries, and direct links to the documents. Go to
https://www.ferc.gov/​ferc-online/​overview
to register for eSubscription.
For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact the Office of Public Participation at (202) 502-6595 or
OPP@ferc.gov
.
Additional information about the Project is available from the FERC website (
www.ferc.gov
). Using the “eLibrary” link, select “General Search” from the eLibrary menu, enter the selected date range and “Docket Number” excluding the last three digits (
i.e.,
CP26-572), and follow the instructions. For assistance with access to eLibrary, the helpline can be reached at (866) 208-3676, TTY (202) 502-8659, or at
FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
.
The eLibrary link on the FERC website also provides access to the texts of formal documents issued by the Commission, such as orders, notices, and rule makings.
(Authority:
18 CFR 2.1
)
Dated: November 19, 2026.
Debbie-Anne A. Reese,
Secretary.

new
combined cycle gas turbine plant receiving up to 123,000 MMcf/d from Southern Star. This Notice of Schedule reflects the correct project description.

, the Commission's deadline for other agency's decisions applies unless a schedule is otherwise established by federal law.

Take notice that on November 6, 2026, Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc. (EGTS), 10700 Energy Way, Glen Allen, VA 23060, filed an application under section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (NGA) and Part 157 of the Commission's regulations requesting authorization for its Project Stratum (Project). EGTS proposes to construct approximately 1.8 miles of new 24-inch diameter pipeline in Beaver County, PA; approximately 13.8 miles of 24-inch diameter replacement pipeline in Clinton and Potter Counties, PA; a new Metering and Regulation (M&R) facility (New Terrain) in Lawrence County, PA; two new gate facilities in Potter and Beaver Counties, PA (Pine Mountain and Eaglerock stations respectively) and various improvements at existing Sabinsville, Leidy, Greenlick, and Kopple Junction stations in Tioga, Clinton, Potter and Beaver Counties respectively. The Project will enable EGTS to provide 250,000 dekatherms per day of additional firm natural gas transportation service from Tioga County to delivery points in Lawrence and Clinton Counties, Pennsylvania. EGTS estimates the total cost of the Project to be $163,008,090 and proposes to provide service under its existing firm transportation rate schedule, all as more fully set forth in the application which is on file with the Commission and open for public inspection.
In addition to publishing the full text of this document in the
Federal Register
, the Commission provides all interested persons an opportunity to view and/or print the contents of this document via the internet through the Commission's Home Page (
http://www.ferc.gov
). From the Commission's Home Page on the internet, this information is available on eLibrary. The full text of this document is available on eLibrary in PDF and Microsoft Word format for viewing, printing, and/or downloading. To access this document in eLibrary, type the docket number excluding the last three digits of this document in the docket number field.
User assistance is available for eLibrary and the Commission's website during normal business hours from FERC Online Support at (202) 502-6652 (toll free at 1-866-208-3676) or email at
(
printed page 75844)
ferconlinesupport@ferc.gov
,
or the Public Reference Room at (202) 502-8371, TTY (202) 502-8659. Email the Public Reference Room at
public.referenceroom@ferc.gov
.
Any questions regarding the proposed project should be directed to Grace Pietro, Associate Regulatory Analyst, Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc., 10700 Energy Way, Glen Allen, VA 23060, by phone at 804-613-5156, or by email at
Grace.Pietro@bhegts.com
.
Pursuant to section 157.9 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure,
[
1
]
within 90 days of this Notice the Commission staff will either: complete its environmental review and place it into the Commission's public record (eLibrary) for this proceeding; or issue a Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review. If a Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review is issued, it will indicate, among other milestones, the anticipated date for the Commission staff's issuance of the final environmental impact statement (FEIS) or environmental assessment (EA) for this proposal. The filing of an EA in the Commission's public record for this proceeding or the issuance of a Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review will serve to notify federal and state agencies of the timing for the completion of all necessary reviews, and the subsequent need to complete all federal authorizations within 90 days of the date of issuance of the Commission staff's FEIS or EA.
Water Quality Certification
EGTS stated that a water quality certificate under section 401 of the Clean Water Act is required for the project from Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection Regional Permitting Coordination Office. When available, EGTS should submit to the Commission a copy of the request for certification for the Commission authorization, including the date the request was submitted to the certifying agency, and either (1) a copy of the certifying agency's decision or (2) evidence of waiver of water quality certification.
Public Participation
There are three ways to become involved in the Commission's review of this project: you can file comments on the project, you can protest the filing, and you can file a motion to intervene in the proceeding. There is no fee or cost for filing comments or intervening. The deadline for filing a motion to intervene is 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 10, 2026. How to file protests, motions to intervene, and comments is explained below.
For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact the Office of Public Participation (OPP) at (202) 502-6595 or
OPP@ferc.gov
.
Comments
Any person wishing to comment on the project may do so. Comments may include statements of support or objections, to the project as a whole or specific aspects of the project. The more specific your comments, the more useful they will be.
Protests
Pursuant to sections 157.10(a)(4)
[
2
]
and 385.211
[
3
]
of the Commission's regulations under the NGA, any person
[
4
]
may file a protest to the application. Protests must comply with the requirements specified in section 385.2001
[
5
]
of the Commission's regulations. A protest may also serve as a motion to intervene so long as the protestor states it also seeks to be an intervenor.
To ensure that your comments or protests are timely and properly recorded, please submit your comments on or before
5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 10, 2026.
There are three methods you can use to submit your comments or protests to the Commission. In all instances, please reference the Project docket number CP27-13-000 in your submission.
(1) You may file your comments electronically by using the eComment feature, which is located on the Commission's website at
www.ferc.gov
under the link to Documents and Filings. Using eComment is an easy method for interested persons to submit brief, text-only comments on a project;
(2) You may file your comments or protests electronically by using the eFiling feature, which is located on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov
)
under the link to Documents and Filings. With eFiling, you can provide comments in a variety of formats by attaching them as a file with your submission. New eFiling users must first create an account by clicking on “eRegister.” You will be asked to select the type of filing you are making; first select “General” and then select “Comment on a Filing”; or
(3) You can file a paper copy of your comments or protests by mailing them to the following address below. Your written comments must reference the Project docket number (CP27-13-000).
To file via USPS:
Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Washington, DC 20426.
To file via any other courier:
Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, Maryland 20852.
The Commission encourages electronic filing of comments (options 1 and 2 above) and has eFiling staff available to assist you at (202) 502-8258 or
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
.
Persons who comment on the environmental review of this project will be placed on the Commission's environmental mailing list, and will receive notification when the environmental documents (EA or EIS) are issued for this project and will be notified of meetings associated with the Commission's environmental review process.
The Commission considers all comments received about the project in determining the appropriate action to be taken.
However, the filing of a comment alone will not serve to make the filer a party to the proceeding.
To become a party, you must intervene in the proceeding. For instructions on how to intervene, see below.
Interventions
Any person, which includes individuals, organizations, businesses, municipalities, and other entities,
[
6
]
has the option to file a motion to intervene in this proceeding. Only intervenors have the right to request rehearing of Commission orders issued in this proceeding and to subsequently challenge the Commission's orders in the U.S. Circuit Courts of Appeal.
To intervene, you must submit a motion to intervene to the Commission in accordance with Rule 214 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure
[
7
]
and the regulations under the NGA
[
8
]
by the intervention deadline for the project, which is
5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 10, 2026.
As described further in Rule 214, your motion to intervene must state, to the extent known, your position regarding the proceeding, as well as your interest in the proceeding. For an individual, this could include your status as a landowner, ratepayer, resident of an
(
printed page 75845)
impacted community, or recreationist. You do not need to have property directly impacted by the project in order to intervene. For more information about motions to intervene, refer to the FERC website at
https://www.ferc.gov/​resources/​guides/​how-to/​intervene.asp
.
There are two ways to submit your motion to intervene. In both instances, please reference the Project docket number CP27-13-000 in your submission.
(1) You may file your motion to intervene by using the Commission's eFiling feature, which is located on the Commission's website (
www.ferc.gov
)
under the link to Documents and Filings. New eFiling users must first create an account by clicking on “eRegister.” You will be asked to select the type of filing you are making; first select “General” and then select “Intervention.” The eFiling feature includes a document-less intervention option; for more information, visit
https://www.ferc.gov/​docs-filing/​efiling/​document-less-intervention.pdf.
;
or
(2) You can file a paper copy of your motion to intervene, along with three copies, by mailing the documents to the address below. Your motion to intervene must reference the Project docket number CP27-13-000.
To file via USPS:
Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Washington, DC 20426.
To file via any other courier:
Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 12225 Wilkins Avenue, Rockville, Maryland 20852.
The Commission encourages electronic filing of motions to intervene (option 1 above) and has eFiling staff available to assist you at (202) 502-8258 or
FercOnlineSupport@ferc.gov
.
Protests and motions to intervene must be served on the applicant either by mail at: Grace Pietro, Associate Regulatory Analyst, Eastern Gas Transmission and Storage, Inc., 10700 Energy Way, Glen Allen, VA 23060 or by email (with a link to the document) at
Grace.Pietro@bhegts.com
.
Any subsequent submissions by an intervenor must be served on the applicant and all other parties to the proceeding. Contact information for parties can be downloaded from the service list at the eService link on FERC Online. Service can be via email with a link to the document.
All timely, unopposed
[
9
]
motions to intervene are automatically granted by operation of Rule 214(c)(1).
[
10
]
Motions to intervene that are filed after the intervention deadline are untimely, and may be denied. Any late-filed motion to intervene must show good cause for being late and must explain why the time limitation should be waived and provide justification by reference to factors set forth in Rule 214(d) of the Commission's Rules and Regulations.
[
11
]
A person obtaining party status will be placed on the service list maintained by the Secretary of the Commission and will receive copies (paper or electronic) of all documents filed by the applicant and by all other parties.
Tracking the Proceeding
Throughout the proceeding, additional information about the project will be available from OPP at (202) 502-6595 or on the FERC website at
www.ferc.gov
using the “eLibrary” link as described above. The eLibrary link also provides access to the texts of all formal documents issued by the Commission, such as orders, notices, and rulemakings.
In addition, the Commission offers a free service called eSubscription which allows you to keep track of all formal issuances and submittals in specific dockets. This can reduce the amount of time you spend researching proceedings by automatically providing you with notification of these filings, document summaries, and direct links to the documents. For more information and to register, go to
www.ferc.gov/​docs-filing/​esubscription.asp
.
Intervention Deadline:
5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 10, 2026.

Take notice that on November 9, 2026, Columbia Gas Transmission, LLC (Columbia), located at 700 Louisiana Street, Suite 1300, Houston, Texas 77002-2700, filed in the above referenced docket, a prior notice request pursuant to sections 157.205 and 157.208 of the Commission's regulations under the Natural Gas Act (NGA), and Columbia's blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP83-76-000, for authorization to install launchers and receivers and to modify other appurtenant facilities to enable pigging activities on its 24-inch-diameter pipeline (Line D415) located in Richland, Crawford, Huron, and Seneca Counties, Ohio (Line D415 Make Piggable Segment 1 Project). AM-69, AM-25, AM-98, AM-107, and KM-43. The facilities are located in Saline, Dallas, and Cleveland Counties, Arkansas respectively. (2026-Q4 MAOP Reduction Project). The project will allow EGT to maintain compliance with Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration regulations and provide more efficient operations of the delivery facilities. The proposed MAOP reductions will also allow EGT to avoid unnecessary expenses associated with hydrotesting, lateral pipe replacement, and other measures that would otherwise be required to maintain the existing MAOP. No construction or modification of facilities is proposed, and therefore, no construction costs are associated with the proposed MAOP reductions, all as more fully set forth in the request, which is on file with the Commission and open to public inspection.

Department of Energy
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
[Project No. 2943-007]
On July 6, 2026, the City of Columbus, Ohio (exemptee) filed an application for surrender of exemption from licensing for the O'Shaughnessy Dam Hydroelectric Facility Project No. 2943. The project is located on the Scioto River, in Delaware County, Ohio. The project does not occupy federal lands.
The exemptee proposes to surrender its exemption from licensing and decommission the project by sealing off the intakes and backfilling all major components with cementitious materials and securing the site by placing fill within the existing structure walls. The dam and reservoir would remain in place to provide the water supply for the City of Columbus, Ohio.
On September 28, 2026, the Commission issued a Notice of Application for Surrender of Exemption Accepted for Filing and Soliciting Comments, Motions to Intervene, and Protest. No stakeholders submitted comments.
This notice identifies Commission staff's intention to prepare an environmental assessment (EA) under the National Environmental Policy Act (
42 U.S.C. 4321
et seq)
for the project.
[
1
]
Commission staff plans to issue an EA by June 25, 2027.
Commission staff may revise the schedule as appropriate. Commission staff will issue the EA for a 30-day comment period and will review all comments filed on the EA and consider them in the Commission's final decision on the proceeding.
For public inquiries and assistance with making filings such as interventions, comments, or requests for rehearing, contact the Office of Public Participation at (202) 502-6595 or
OPP@ferc.gov
.

.

Attachment—Exemption
NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION
Docket Nos. 52-025 and 52-026
Southern Nuclear Operating Company
Vogtle Electric Generating Plant, Units 3 and 4
Exemptions
I. Background.
Southern Nuclear Operating Company (SNC, the licensee) is the holder of Combined License Nos. NPF-91 and NPF-92 for the Vogtle Electric Generating Plant (Vogtle), Units 3 and 4, respectively. The licenses state, among other things, that the licensee is subject to all rules, regulations, and orders of the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC, the Commission) now or hereafter in effect. These facilities consist of two pressurized-water reactors located at the licensee's site in Burke County, Georgia, respectively.
On July 17, 2024, NRC issued a final rule incorporating by reference Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.147, “Inservice Inspection Code Case Acceptability, ASME Section XI, Division 1,” Revision 21 (Agencywide Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS), Accession No. ML23291A003), into Title 10 of the
Code of Federal Regulations
(10 CFR) 50.55a(3)(ii) (
89 FR 58039
). This RG determined American Society of Mechanical Engineers Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code, Section XI (ASME BPV XI) Code Case N-921, “Alternative 12-yr Inspection Interval Duration, Section XI, Division 1,” to be conditionally acceptable. This code case allows NRC licensees to implement an inservice inspection (ISI) program based upon a 12-year ISI interval, as opposed to the traditional 10-year ISI interval required by ASME BPV XI, Article IWA- 2431. RG 1.147, Revision 21, specifies four conditions on Code Case N-921.
Condition 2 states, “This code case can only be implemented at the beginning of an ISI interval as part of a routine update of the ISI program.” The July 17, 2024, final rule also added
10 CFR 50.55a(y)
, which includes a definition for the term “inservice inspection interval.” This definition, in part, specifies that the length of the ISI interval is described in ASME BPV XI, Article IWA-2431.
II. Action.
By application dated April 27, 2026 (ML26117A373), the licensee, pursuant to
10 CFR 50.12
, “Specific exemptions,” requested exemptions from certain requirements of
10 CFR 50.55a(a)(3)(ii)
and
10 CFR 50.55a(y)
to allow the use of Code Case N-921 after the start dates of the first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, which is not in accordance with Condition 2 on Code Case N-921, as specified in RG 1.147, Revision 21. The first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, began on July 31, 2023, and April 29, 2024, respectively. The end of the current 10-year first ISI interval is July 30, 2033, and April 28, 2034, for Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, respectively. The end of the proposed 12-year first ISI interval is July 30, 2035, and April 28, 2036, for Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, respectively. The licensee stated that the ASME Section XI Code of Record for the Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, first ISI Interval is the 2019 Edition. The licensee stated that the Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, augmented inspection examination schedules will remain unchanged. The licensee also stated that the exceptions of IWB-2411(a), IWC-2411(a) and IWD-2411(a) will be applied to Table 1 of Code Case N-921 when implemented.
III. Discussion.
Pursuant to
10 CFR 50.12(a)
, the Commission may, upon application by any interested person or upon its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of
10 CFR part 50
when (1) the exemptions are authorized by law, will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety, and are consistent with the common defense and security and (2) special circumstances are present. Under
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)
, special circumstances
(
printed page 75887)
are present when at least one of the following six conditions are met:
(i) Application of the regulation in the particular circumstances conflicts with other rules or requirements of the Commission; or
(ii) Application of the regulation in the particular circumstances would not serve the underlying purpose of the rule or is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose of the rule; or
(iii) Compliance would result in undue hardship or other costs that are significantly in excess of those contemplated when the regulation was adopted, or that are significantly in excess of those incurred by others similarly situated; or
(iv) The exemption would result in benefit to the public health and safety that compensates for any decrease in safety that may result from the grant of the exemption; or
(v) The exemption would provide only temporary relief from the applicable regulation and the licensee or applicant has made good faith efforts to comply with the regulation; or
(vi) There is present any other material circumstance not considered when the regulation was adopted for which it would be in the public interest to grant an exemption.
A. The Exemptions are Authorized by Law
The exemptions would authorize exemption from certain requirements of
10 CFR 50.55a(a)(3)(ii)
and
10 CFR 50.55a(y)
to allow the use of Code Case N-921, after the start dates of the first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4. As stated,
10 CFR 50.12(a)
allows the NRC to grant an exemption from the requirements of
10 CFR part 50
, including
10 CFR 50.55a(a)(3)(ii)
and
10 CFR 50.55a(y)
, when the exemption is authorized by law. Exemption is authorized by law where it is not expressly prohibited by statute or regulation. Proposed exemptions are implicitly authorized by law if it will not present an undue risk to public health and safety, is consistent with the common defense and security, and special circumstances are present, and no other provisions in law prohibit, or otherwise restrict, its application. The NRC staff has determined that no provisions in law expressly prohibit or otherwise restrict the application of the requested exemptions. The NRC staff has also determined, as explained below, that the requested exemptions will not present an undue risk to public health and safety, is consistent with the common defense and security, and special circumstances are present. Therefore, the NRC staff concludes that the exemptions are authorized by law.
B. The Exemptions Present No Undue Risk to Public Health and Safety
These exemptions would allow the licensee to implement Code Case N-921 after the start dates of the first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4. The first interval for Vogtle, Unit 3, began July 31, 2023 and on April 29, 2024 for Vogle, Unit 4. The action does not change the manner in which the plant operates and maintains public health and safety because the exemptions do not result in a change to the facility or the current operating license. The licensee stated that extending the ISI interval by two years does not impact the technical basis supporting any of the currently authorized
10 CFR 50.55a
alternatives and does not create any particular challenge in reconciling the ISI inspection schedules to conform with the three four-year periods specified in Code Case N-921. Accordingly, the NRC staff reviewed the alternatives listed in Attachment 2 of the licensee's exemption request dated April 27, 2026, for ISI interval-related impacts and identified several common themes in these alternatives and evaluated the alternatives as described below.
The NRC noted that the following previously authorized alternatives/relief requests were based on a 10-year ISI interval for which SNC performed a review, as described in the letter dated April 27, 2026, and assessed the impact of extending the interval by 2 years to implement Code Case N-921 on the technical basis supporting each alternative.
VEGP 3&4—PSI/ISI-ALT-06—April 25, 2019 (ML19087A173)
VEGP 3&4—PSI/ISI-ALT-08—March 26, 2018 (ML18071A359)
VEGP 3&4—PSI/ISI-ALT-14R1—September 17, 2020 (ML20147A663)
VEGP 3&4—PSI-ISI-ALT-15R1—April 9, 2021 (ML21090A247)
VEGP 3&4—ISI-ALT-17—April 14, 2023 (Package, ML23095A284)
VEGP 3&4—ISI1-ALT-18—May 4, 2023 (Package, ML23109A067)
VEGP 3&4—ISI-ALT-2025-01—July 24, 2025 (ML25196A297)
Alternatives With No ISI Interval Relationship
NRC staff noted that the results of SNC's assessment determined that there is no impact on the technical basis supporting any of the previously approved alternatives. For example, the previously approved alternatives approved include: inspection of the pipe base material and weld from the pipe side in lieu of a volumetric inspection; use of alternative counterbore configurations on weld joints; alternative flaw acceptance criteria; reduced coverage due to inaccessibility; visual inspection in lieu of volumetric sections for inner radius sections of specific reactor vessel nozzles; and utilization of a later edition of the ASME Code, Section XI. Therefore, the NRC staff's basis for approving the previously approved alternatives listed above are not impacted by extending the length of the ISI interval to 12 years.
Based on its review of the licensee's analysis of alternatives in Enclosure 2 of the exemption request, dated April 27, 2026, the NRC staff concludes that the exemptions would not result in any significant reduction in the effectiveness of the ISI programs implemented by the licensee at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4. Further, based on the above, the NRC staff concludes that the exemptions would not present an undue risk to the public health and safety.
C. The Exemptions are Consistent With the Common Defense and Security
The requested exemptions would allow the licensee to implement Code Case N-921 after the start dates of the first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4. The change is administrative in nature, adequately controlled by the ISI Program criteria and ASME Code requirements and is not related to security issues. The length of the ISI interval is also not related to security issues. Thus, NRC staff determined that the common defense and security is not impacted by this exemption, and, therefore, the exemptions are consistent with the common defense and security.
D. Special Circumstances
The regulation under
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)
states, in part, that “[t]he Commission will not consider granting an exemption unless special circumstances are present,” and describes, in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(i)
—(vi), the conditions under which special circumstances exist.
In the licensee's exemption request submittal dated April 27, 2026, the licensee stated that three of the six special circumstances listed in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)
are present:
(ii) Application of the regulation in the particular circumstances would not serve the underlying purpose of the rule or is not necessary to achieve the underlying purpose of the rule.
(iii) Compliance would result in undue hardship or other costs that are significantly in excess of those contemplated when the regulation was
(
printed page 75888)
adopted, or that are significantly in excess of those incurred by others similarly situated.
(vi) There is present any other material circumstance not considered when the regulation was adopted for which it would be in the public interest to grant an exemption.
The NRC staff performed an independent review of the special circumstances claimed by the licensee.
For the special circumstances in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii)
, the licensee stated that the purpose of the July 2024 final rule (
89 FR 58039
) was to identify ASME Code cases that the NRC determined to be acceptable for use. The licensee noted that NRC's approval of Code Case N-921 includes a condition that, “This code case can only be implemented at the beginning of an ISI interval as part of a routine update of the ISI program.” The licensee provided the following support to the claim that application of the regulation would not serve the underlying purpose of the rule:
The licensee stated: “Implementation of Code Case N-921 during the current ISI interval (and the first of three periods within the interval) does not inhibit the ability to comply with code required periodic distribution requirements and allows for a more consistent periodic distribution of examinations and tests throughout the extended interval.”
Tables 2 and 3 for Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, of the licensee's submittal dated April 27, 2026, described the new inspection period dates and corresponding refueling outages.
The licensee evaluated all NRC-authorized alternative requests in the enclosure of the licensee's submittal, dated April 27, 2026, consistent with NRC concerns expressed in the
89 FR 58039
final rule preamble (see NRC staff's independent review above).
The licensee stated that the site ISI program owners routinely modify the ISI examination schedule during the ISI interval due to various reasons, such as evolving availability of qualified personnel and equipment.
In the
89 FR 58039
final rule preamble, the NRC communicated that order and predictability of licensee ISI programs is a paramount consideration. The careful advance planning required by ASME BPV XI and
10 CFR 50.55a
maximizes licensee effectiveness in successfully executing all ISI requirements. The successful execution of ISI requirements, in turn, contributes to nuclear safety by providing a data stream used to continuously evaluate the structural integrity of safety-related components. The NRC staff determined that the licensee provided adequate evidence that, if the NRC staff approves the proposed exemptions, the ISI programs at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4, will be managed in a manner that promotes order and predictability.
In the
89 FR 58039
final rule, the NRC added a new condition requiring that Code Case N-921 be implemented at the start of a new ISI interval. The basis for the condition is that implementation of Code Case N-921 in the middle of an ISI interval creates complications related to existing examination schedules and alternatives that were approved assuming a 10-year ISI interval. As discussed above, the licensee demonstrated that no currently approved alternatives are impacted by extending the length of the ISI interval to 12 years. Another concern identified by the NRC staff with allowing mid-cycle implementation of Code Case N-921 involves potential complications of reconciling ISI inspection schedules to conform with the three four-year periods specified in Code Case N-921. As discussed above, the licensee stated that in anticipation of implementing Code Case N-921, it proactively adjusted examination schedules accordingly to maintain compliance with Code Case N-921 periodic distribution requirements. Therefore, the NRC staff concludes that application of the regulation would not serve the underlying purpose of the rule because the licensee demonstrated that mid-cycle implementation of Code Case N-921 will have no impact on the ISI programs at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4. Based on the above, the NRC staff determined that the special circumstances described in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(ii)
are present for the requested exemption. Since the regulations require that one of the special circumstances in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)
be satisfied before NRC may grant an exemption, the NRC staff did not evaluate the licensee's additional claims that the special circumstances in
10 CFR 50.12(a)(2)(iii)
and
(vi)
are also applicable.
E. Environmental Considerations
The NRC staff determined that the exemptions discussed herein meets the eligibility criteria for categorical exclusion set forth in
10 CFR 51.22(d)(1)
due to changes to requirements in
10 CFR part 50
or
52
with respect to changes to inspection or surveillance requirements, because the changes do not provide any ground disturbance and there is no significant change in the types or significant increase in the amounts of any effluents that may be released offsite, no significant increase in individual or cumulative public or occupational radiation exposure, and no significant increase in the potential for or consequences from radiological accidents. Therefore, in accordance with
10 CFR 51.22(d)
, no environmental impact statement or environmental assessment need to be prepared in connection with the issuance of these exemptions.
The basis for this NRC staff determination is discussed as follows with an evaluation against each of the requirements in
10 CFR 51.22(d)
.
There is no significant hazards consideration.
The criteria for determining whether an action involves a significant hazards consideration are found in
10 CFR 50.92(c)
. The exemptions only involve an ISI program implementation change, which is administrative in nature. The exemptions do not adversely affect plant equipment, operation, or procedures. Therefore, there are no significant hazard considerations, because granting the exemptions would not: (1) involve a significant increase in the probability or consequences of an accident previously evaluated; or (2) create the possibility of a new or different kind of accident from any accident previously evaluated; or (3) involve a significant reduction in a margin of safety.
There is no significant change in the types or significant increase in the amounts of any effluents that may be released offsite.
The exemptions involve only an ISI program implementation change, which is administrative in nature, and does not involve any changes in the types or significant increase in the amounts of any effluents that may be released offsite.
There is no significant increase in individual or cumulative public or occupational radiation exposure.
Since the exemptions involve only an ISI program implementation change, which is administrative in nature, it does not contribute to any significant increase in occupational or public radiation exposure.
There is no significant construction impact.
Since the exemptions involve only an ISI program implementation change, which is administrative in nature, it does not involve any construction impact.
There is no significant increase in the potential for or consequences from radiological accidents.
The exemptions involve only an ISI program implementation change, which is administrative in nature and does not impact the potential for or consequences from accidents.
(
printed page 75889)
The requirements from which the exemption is sought involve requirements that are of an administrative, managerial, or organizational nature.
The exemptions involve only an ISI program implementation change regarding examination scheduling requirements and other requirements of an administrative, managerial, or organizational nature, because it is associated with the marginal extension from a 10-year to 12-year ISI interval.
Based on the above, NRC staff determined that the exemptions meet the eligibility criteria for the categorical exclusion set forth in
10 CFR 51.22(d)(1)
. Therefore, in accordance with
10 CFR 51.22(d)
, no environmental impact statement or environmental assessment need to be prepared in connection with these exemptions requests.
IV. Conclusions
Accordingly, the Commission has determined that, pursuant to
10 CFR 50.12
, the exemptions are authorized by law, will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety, and are consistent with the common defense and security. Also, special circumstances are present. Therefore, the Commission hereby grants SNC's request for exemptions from certain requirements of
10 CFR 50.55a(a)(3)(ii)
and
10 CFR 50.55a(y)
to allow the implementation of ASME Code Case N-921 after the start date of the first ISI interval at Vogtle, Units 3 and 4.
The exemptions are effective upon issuance.

Department of Veterans Affairs
38 CFR Part 77
[Docket No. VA-2026-VHA-0496]
RIN 2900-AS64
AGENCY:
Department of Veterans Affairs.
ACTION:
Proposed rule.
SUMMARY:
This proposed rule would amend the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations that govern grants for adaptive sports programs for disabled veterans and disabled members of the armed forces to allow for a more efficient review and selection of applicants for the grant. This rule would ensure that the grant aligns with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards by requiring applicants to submit an application within the VA established deadline for submission; requiring that all adaptive sports grants be openly competed; and adding a new section on appropriate actions VA may take to enforce this part. The changes proposed by this rulemaking will improve program administration without negatively impacting the veteran athletes supported by these grants.
DATES:
Comments must be received on or before January 25, 2027.
ADDRESSES:
You may submit comments through
www.regulations.gov
under RIN 2900-AS64. That website includes a plain-language summary of this rulemaking. Comments will be posted for viewing by the public on
www.regulations.gov
,
including any personally identifiable information (
e.g.,
a social security number or address) within a comment and its supporting materials. However, VA retains discretion to redact personal or sensitive information, including but not limited to personal or sensitive information pertaining to third parties. Additionally, VA will not post public comments that make threats to individuals or institutions or suggest that the commenter will take actions to harm an individual. Instructions for accessing agency documents, submitting comments, and viewing the rulemaking docket, are available on

Rachel McArdle, Deputy Executive Director, VHA Rehabilitation Prosthetics Service, (727) 219-6296. (This is not a toll-free telephone number.)
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
I. Background
Section 521A of title 38, United States Code (U.S.C.) provides that the Secretary may carry out a program under which the Secretary may make grants to eligible entities for planning, developing, managing, and implementing programs to provide adaptive sports opportunities for disabled veterans and disabled members of the Armed Forces (adaptive sports grants). On July 1, 2014, VA established regulations in
part 77 of title 38, Code of Federal Regulations
(CFR) to establish the adaptive sports grant program. See 79
Federal Register
(FR) 37211. As described in detail below, VA proposes to amend these regulations by making both substantive changes and technical corrections to part 77. These changes would align this part with the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards at
2 CFR part 200
and with other VA and Federal grant programs.
II. Substantive Changes to
38 CFR Part 77
A. Proposed Removal of § 77.6 Amendments to Grant Applications
In this rulemaking VA proposes to remove § 77.6, which establishes that an applicant may seek an amendment to its grant application after the deadline for submission and establishes the requirements for amending an application before or after the submission deadline. This change is necessary to comply with the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) Memorandum M-04-01, Memorandum for Heads of Executive Departments and Agencies, dated October 15, 2003, which directs all Federal grant-making agencies to publish funding opportunity announcements—called “synopses”—on
Grants.gov
. This website views each application as a separate entry and does not allow an applicant to use the process described in current § 77.6 to amend an application package after the package has been submitted. If an applicant wants to amend an application, the applicant must resubmit a complete application package prior to the submission deadline (and not an amendment limited to the individual documents currently listed in § 77.6). A resubmission is needed because the electronic application portal does not allow the applicant to access their prior application package once the application is submitted. VA will continue to allow applicants to resubmit complete grant applications with updated documents prior to the deadline, even after this proposed rule becomes final. However, VA will not accept resubmitted complete applications after the submission deadline because the application portal closes at the submission deadline.
In addition to the technical limitations, with the growth of the grant program, allowing submission of revised applications after the application deadline and during the review process creates an administrative burden that prevents VA from being able to fully review all grant applications within a reasonable time period. In turn, this results in potential delay in the award and distribution of grants.
Further, removing current § 77.6 would be consistent with other grant programs, such as VA Homeless Grant and Per Diem and Supportive Services for Veteran Families Program (see part 62 of
chapter I of Title 38 of the Code of Federal Regulations
), which do not allow for amendment of applications after the deadline for their submission.
For these reasons, VA proposes to remove current § 77.6. VA would not replace the current language with revised language.
B. Proposed Removal of Noncompetitive Adaptive Sports Grants
The current adaptive sports grants regulations allow for noncompetitive grants. Current § 77.13 provides that when VA identifies that an eligible entity is the only entity capable of providing an adaptive sports activity and VA determines that the award of a grant to this entity is warranted to enable adaptive sports activities, VA may request that entity to submit a grant application. Current § 77.4(c) establishes the application process for these noncompetitive grants. Further, §§ 77.9 and 77.10(a) address the use of pre-applications for noncompetitive grant applications and VA's use of a peer review process when reviewing noncompetitive grant applications, respectively.
In this rulemaking, VA proposes to remove all regulation text that authorizes or governs noncompetitive grants to ensure that VA complies with
2 CFR 200.204
, by establishing that adaptive sports grant awards are openly competed and there is an equal opportunity for funding under this grant mechanism to all applicants. Section 200.204 provides that a Federal agency must announce specific funding opportunities for Federal financial assistance that will be openly competed. The term “openly competed” means opportunities that are not directed to one or more specifically identified applicants.
Therefore, VA proposes to remove § 77.13 in its entirety, § 77.4(c), and the references to noncompetitive grants in § 77.9 and § 77.10(a).
C. Proposed Amendment of Current § 77.21
Current § 77.21 is titled “Application of other regulations” and states that for purposes of this part, the requirements in
38 CFR parts 43
and
49
are superseded by those in
2 CFR part 200
. In this rulemaking, VA proposes to remove the current title and regulation text because
38 CFR parts 43
and
49
have been removed, thereby making the language unnecessary. VA will then use § 77.21 to establish remedies for noncompliance when a grantee fails to comply with the grant agreement or this part.
Parts 43 and 49 codified various OMB guidance on cost principals and awards to non-Federal entities in the form of Circulars.
[
1
]
As previously stated in this rulemaking,
2 CFR part 200
establishes the Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal awards to non-Federal entities (Uniform Guidance). On December 19, 2014, OMB published an interim final rule jointly with VA and other Federal Agencies in the
Federal Register
, making corrections to the Uniform Guidance. See
79 FR 75871
. Notably, it added
2 CFR 802.101
, which provided that “The Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards set forth in
2 CFR part 200
shall apply to the Department of Veterans Affairs,” and removed part 43 from 38 CFR. See id. at 76024. For the
(
printed page 75816)
same reasons, VA removed part 49 from 38 CFR in a separate rulemaking. See
80 FR 43320
(Jul. 22, 2015).
VA no longer needs to clarify that the requirements in such parts are superseded by those in
2 CFR part 200
because
38 CFR parts 43
or
49
no longer exist. Therefore, the current provisions of § 77.21 are unnecessary.
Instead of reserving § 77.21 for future use, VA proposes to amend § 77.21 to establish VA's enforcement authority when a grantee fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement or this part. VA proposes to change the title of § 77.21 to “Remedies for noncompliance”. This authority would be consistent with
2 CFR part 200
, specifically,
2 CFR 200.208
(specific conditions), 200.305 (Federal payment), 200.339 through 200.343 (remedies for noncompliance), and 200.346 (collections of amounts due).
Proposed paragraph (a) would state that if a grantee fails to comply with the terms of the grant agreement, VA will enforce this part through actions consistent with
2 CFR part 200
that may include, but are not limited to, withholding, suspension, disallowing costs for all or part of the activity associated with the noncompliance of the grantee, and termination.
VA would explicitly reference
2 CFR part 200
to ensure that grantees know where to locate the remedies VA can use when the grantee is noncompliant. VA refers to
2 CFR part 200
rather than the specific sections, as described above, so that future changes to those sections can be implemented immediately without VA needing to conduct further rulemakings. VA would use withholding, suspension, disallowing costs for all or part of the activity associated with the noncompliance of the grantee, and termination as examples because those are the most common actions VA would take. However, the list is not exhaustive.
VA acknowledges that when certain actions (such as suspension and termination) are taken against grantees pursuant to this section and
2 CFR part 200
, a disruption in services to participants may occur. VA is not proposing to regulate responsibilities for grantees to continue to provide services in circumstances where VA suspends or terminates a grant for adaptive sports programs. Instead, VA will include these requirements in the grant agreement pursuant to part 77. This would ensure that the disruption and impact upon participants is minimized as much as possible.
Proposed paragraph (b) would address recovery of funds by VA. This language is currently in § 77.17; however, VA proposes to move the language to proposed § 77.21(b) because recovery of funds results from a grantee's noncompliance. These recovery provisions would be included in proposed § 77.21, with no revisions to the regulation text. VA would only revise the numbering of the sections in current § 77.17 to conform with the numbering convention in proposed § 77.21. As such, VA would remove § 77.17.
Proposed § 77.21(b) would state that (1) VA may recover from the grantee any funds that are not used in accordance with a grant agreement. If VA decides to recover funds, VA will issue to the grantee a notice of intent to recover grant funds, and grantee will then have 30 days to submit documentation demonstrating why the grant funds should not be recovered. After review of all submitted documentation, VA will determine whether action will be taken to recover the grant funds. (2) When VA makes a final decision that action will be taken to recover grant funds from the grantee, VA must stop further payments of grant funds under this part until the grant funds are recovered and the condition that led to the decision to recover grant funds has been resolved.
D. Proposed Addition of Suspension and Withholding to Definitions in § 77.2
In this rulemaking, VA proposes to add definitions of suspension and withholding to § 77.2 in alphabetical order.
VA proposes to define suspension to mean an action by VA that temporarily withdraws VA funding under an adaptive sports grant, pending corrective action by the grantee or pending a decision to terminate the grant by VA. Suspension of a grant is a separate action from suspension under VA regulations or guidance implementing Executive Orders 12549 and 12689, “Debarment and Suspension.” This definition is consistent with the definition for this term used in other VA grant programs, such as the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program and the Legal Services for Homeless Veterans and Veterans At-Risk for Homelessness Grant Program. See §§ 78.5 and 79.5.
VA proposes to define withholding to mean that an adaptive sports grant will not be paid until VA determines that the grantee has provided sufficient documentation, and/or actions to correct a deficiency, to pay the grant. This definition provides a general description of how this term is used in
2 CFR part 200
. This definition is also generally consistent, with only minor clarifying edits, with how this term is defined in other VA grant programs, such as the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program and the Legal Services for Homeless Veterans and Veterans At-Risk for Homelessness Grant Program. See §§ 78.5 and 79.5.
III. Technical Edits to
38 CFR Part 77
A. Proposed Changes to Terminology Related to Notice of Funding Availability
VA proposes to change the term Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) to Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) throughout part 77. The Federal government, including VA, used these terms at the time VA established the regulations for part 77. However, since that time,
2 CFR 200.204
, which governs discretionary grants and cooperative agreements, including the instant grant program, uses the terminology Notice of Funding Opportunity or NOFO. VA also uses Notice of Funding Opportunity or NOFO in its other grant programs, such as the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program (see
38 CFR 78.110
) and the Legal Services for Homeless Veterans and Veterans At-Risk for Homeless Grant Program (see § 79.65).
To be consistent with § 200.204 and the use of Notice of Funding Opportunity and NOFO in other grant programs VA administers, VA proposes to replace all references in part 77 to “Notice of Funding Availability” with “Notice of Funding Opportunity” and all references to “NOFA” with “NOFO”. Specifically, VA proposes to make these changes to the definition of Notice of Funding Availability in
38 CFR 77.2
,
77.12
Notice of Funding Availability section, and all mentions of NOFA found in 77.3(b), 77.4(a) through (c), 77.5(b), 77.8(a) and (h), 77.9, 77.10(a) and (b), the title and introductory paragraph of § 77.12, and 77.15(a).
These technical edits would not change the meaning of the term and would have no substantive impact.
B. Proposed Changes to Cross References
1. Definition of Adaptive Sports Grant Agreement in § 77.2
VA defines the term adaptive sports grant agreement to mean the agreement executed between VA and a grantee as specified under § 77.17. VA made a technical error in citing to § 77.17, which authorizes VA to recover funds from the grantee if they are not used in accordance with an adaptive sports grant agreement. Section 77.14 describes grant agreements for this program. Thus,
(
printed page 75817)
VA proposes to make a technical revision to the definition of adaptive sports grant agreement in § 77.2 by removing the reference to § 77.17 and adding, in its place, § 77.14. This revision has no substantive impact on the definition of adaptive sports grant agreement.
2. Definition of Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO)
VA currently defines the term Notice of Funding Availability to mean a Notice of Funding Availability published in the OMB-designated government-wide website in accordance with § 77.13 and
2 CFR part 200
. As previously stated in this rulemaking, VA proposes to revise the term Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) to Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) throughout part 77. In addition to making this revision, VA would also make a technical revision to the definition of NOFO. VA made a technical error in citing to § 77.13 because this section addresses applications for noncompetitive adaptive sports grants, not NOFOs; section 77.12 addresses NOFOs. Thus, VA proposes to make a technical revision to the definition of NOFO in § 77.2 by removing the reference to § 77.13 and adding, in its place, § 77.12. This revision would have no substantive impact on the definition of NOFO.
3. Definition of Peer Review
VA currently defines the term peer review to mean “the technical and programmatic evaluation by a group of experts qualified by training and experience to give expert advice, based on selection criteria established under § 77.13 or in a program announcement, on the technical and programmatic merit of adaptive sports grant applications.”
38 CFR 77.2
. VA made a technical error in citing to § 77.13, which addresses applications for noncompetitive adaptive sports grants, not selection criteria. Section 77.12 is the appropriate citation because it addresses NOFOs and the NOFO provides for the selection criteria. Thus, VA proposes to make a technical revision to the definition of peer review in § 77.2 by removing the reference to § 77.13 and adding, in its place, § 77.12. This revision would have no substantive impact on the definition of peer review.
3. Definition of Veteran in § 77.2
VA proposes to revise the definition of veteran in § 77.2 by citing to
38 U.S.C. 101(2)
instead of
38 CFR 3.1
. Current § 77.2 defines the term “veteran” by adopting the regulatory definition in
38 CFR 3.1
, which, in turn, adopts the statutory definition of veteran in
38 U.S.C. 101(2)
. Referencing the statute ensures that the regulation fully aligns with its statutory authority as well as any future amendments to that statutory authority.
4. Definition of Veterans Service Organization in § 77.2
VA proposes to revise the definition of Veterans Service Organization. VA will technically amend the reference to “
section 5902 of title 38, United States Code
” in the current definition of Veterans Service Organization to simply read “
38 U.S.C. 5902
.” This change is consistent with other statutory references in 38 CFR.
5. Sections 77.4, Applications, and 77.9, Use of Pre-Applications
VA proposes to revise the parenthetical at the end of current § 77.4 that explains that OMB has approved the information collection requirements in this section under control numbers 2900-0820, 4040-0004 for Standard Form 424, and 4040-0008 for Standard Form 424C. VA further proposes to amend the parenthetical at the end of current § 77.9, which describes VA's authority to request pre-application for grant applications and similarly refers to 4040-0008 for Standard Form 424C.
The form associated with the OMB approved number 4040-0008 is Standard Form 424C, which relates to Budget Information for Construction Programs. However, this grant program does not have any provisions for the construction of any type of building. Instead, it should reference Standard Form number 424A, which is Budget Information for Non-Construction Programs and is currently approved by OMB under 4040-0006. Thus, VA proposes to revise the parenthetical of §§ 77.4 and 77.9 to correctly refer to 4040-0006 for Standard Form 424A instead of 4040-0008 for Standard Form 424C. This has no substantive impact on the administration or implementation of §§ 77.4 and 77.9.
6. Section 77.10 Peer Review Methods
Section 77.10 describes VA's use of its internal peer review process when reviewing pre-applications (initial threshold review to determine if the application meets the minimum eligibility criteria) and formal applications for selection of grantees. Both paragraphs (a) and (b) explain that the peer reviewer use the selection criteria in § 77.5. However, § 77.8 also includes requirements that the peer reviewer must take into consideration. Therefore, VA proposes to also include a reference to § 77.8. This would ensure that § 77.10 provides all pertinent references used during the peer review process. This addition has no substantive impact on the administration or implementation of § 77.10.
Executive Orders 12866 and 13563, and 14192
VA examined the impact of this rulemaking as required by Executive Orders 12866 (Sept. 30, 1993) and 13563 (Jan. 18, 2011), which direct agencies to assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives and, if regulation is necessary, to select regulatory approaches that maximize net benefits. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs has determined that this rulemaking is not a significant regulatory action under
Executive Order 12866
, as supplemented by
Executive Order 13563
. Additionally, VA examined this proposed final rule and has determined that it is consistent with the policies and directives outlined in
Executive Order 14192
, Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation (
90 FR 2065
, Feb. 6, 2025), and is considered an
Executive Order 14192
deregulatory action.
Economic Impact:
VA believes this proposed rule is deregulatory because it removes outdated and unused provisions that no longer align with current technology or Federal grants management requirements. By eliminating inefficiencies, the rule streamlines administrative processes and reduces confusion for applicants while improving consistency with other VA grant programs. VA does not anticipate any costs or transfers to be associated with this rule. These changes provide qualitative benefits through improved clarity and efficiency in the adaptive sports grant program.
Regulatory Flexibility Act
The Secretary hereby certifies that this proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities as they are defined in the Regulatory Flexibility Act (
5 U.S.C. 601-612
). The basis for this certification relies on the grant program providing Federal awards (
e.g.,
grant money) to small entities. Although the small entities must apply for Federal awards, there are no out-of-pocket expenses (
e.g.,
no filing fees) created by this rulemaking. Therefore, pursuant to
5 U.S.C. 605(b)
, the initial and final regulatory flexibility analysis requirements of
5 U.S.C. 603
and
604
do not apply.
(
printed page 75818)
Unfunded Mandates
This proposed rule would not result in the expenditure by State, local, and Tribal governments, in the aggregate, or by the private sector, of $100 million or more (adjusted annually for inflation) in any one year.
Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA)
Although this proposed rule contains collection of information under the provisions of the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (
44 U.S.C. 3501-3521
), there are no provisions associated with this rulemaking constituting any new collection of information or any revisions to the existing collection of information. The collections of information for
38 CFR part 77
are found in §§ 77.4, 77.8, 77.9, 77.16, and 77.19. These collections are currently approved by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and have been assigned OMB control numbers 2900-0820, 4040-0004, and 4040-0006. Collections of information are also found in § 77.6. However, that section is proposed to be removed by this rulemaking, and as a result, the reference to collections of information in § 77.6 would also be removed. Additionally, those collections of information in § 77.6 are not currently approved. Thus, the current collections would not be affected by the removal of § 77.6.
