2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
32
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
33
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
34
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
In particular, the Exchange believes the proposed change would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and protect investors and the public interest by making available to investors a type of complex order that incorporates the functionality of a stop-limit order. A stop-limit complex order can effectively be used by a market participant to replace manual monitoring and management a market participant must currently engage in to gain the benefits of stop-limit functionality. As stated previously, the Exchange believes that stop-limit complex orders will generally be utilized by market participants to close existing positions when specific market conditions have been met. Because such situations may arise quickly, stop-limit complex orders provide market participants with an automated way to place the closing order without the manual monitoring that is currently needed, thereby helping to ensure that an order may execute in a timely manner once the desired threshold has been met. Market participants may choose to execute a transaction once certain market conditions are met as a way to help manage and reduce the risk of extreme loss. Stop-limit complex orders provide investors an execution and risk management tool to execute transactions without manually monitoring for certain market conditions (such as when the
(
printed page 75944)
underlying security of a complex instrument is above or below a specific value as determined by the investor, or the price of the complex instrument is above or below a specific value as determined by the investor) and executing transactions when such market conditions are met, as is done today. The introduction of a stop-limit complex order gives market participants who wish to utilize this order type an automated way of monitoring for conditions in which they desire an execution to occur, thereby creating operational efficiencies for the market. The Exchange believes the proposed rules are appropriate in that complex orders are recognized by market participants as useful, both as an investment and a risk management strategy, and adding stop-limit order functionality to complex orders provides even greater utility. The proposed rules will provide an efficient mechanism for carrying out investor strategies.
The Exchange also believes auctioning triggered stop-limit complex orders through a SCOA will provide those orders with additional opportunities for price improvement and executions, particularly given that multiple stop-limit complex orders may be triggered by the same event. SCOA is necessary as a new auction mechanism to accommodate stop-limit complex order auctions because SCOA functionality that bundles multiple orders is unique to the SCOA auction mechanism. The Exchange believes that when multiple stop-limit complex orders are triggered by the same event, bundling into a single SCOA will have better execution outcomes than processing multiple individual orders in separate auctions, as a single auction message will be most efficient for those receiving and responding to the auction message, rather than having to process multiple messages in a very small time interval. Further, the SCOA allocation method is unique and designed to maximize the number of contracts executed, which is important because stop-limit orders are intended specifically to mitigate risk upon the occurrence of a triggering market condition and provide benefit only if executed upon observation of the triggering event. A stop-limit order that is triggered and does not receive an execution may leave the customer with an open position that was intended to be closed upon a triggering event. Thus, maximizing the number of contracts executed at the conclusion of a SCOA is of high importance. Pursuant to the proposed trigger process, the System will initiate the SCOA process for all stop-limit complex orders once designated conditions are met. Through the SCOA process, the Exchange intends to allocate resting interest and auction responses against auctioned stop-limit orders to maximize executed volume, thereby filling stop-limit complex orders to the extent possible based on the auction responses received for the SCOA and resting interest in the COB. The Exchange believes this allocation method will benefit investors because it will result in execution of as many contracts of the auctioned order(s) as possible. The Exchange believes that the proposal to initiate a SCOA once the designated trigger condition for a stop-limit complex order has been met removes impediments to, and perfects the mechanisms of, a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protects investors and the public interest because the Exchange will initiate a SCOA for a stop-limit complex order in accordance with the User's instructions. Additionally, through the SCOA functionality that bundles multiple stop-limit complex orders with the same trigger condition into the same SCOA, SCOA processing will pursue price improvement through its allocation algorithm that is designed to maximize execution quantity while optimizing price-improvement opportunities for customers. The proposed execution of SCOA orders following the conclusion of a SCOA is consistent with general principles of customer priority and protects the leg markets. While SCOA orders may execute against complex contra-side interest only, the prices of these executions must improve the SBBO if there is a Priority Customer representing any leg on the Simple Book as required by Rule 5.33(f)(2)(A)(iv). SCOA order execution must comply with all requirements for execution prices in Rule 5.33(f)(2)(A). The proposed stop-limit complex order rules also promote equal access by providing recipients of the Exchange's data feeds that include auction notifications with the opportunity to interact with orders in a SCOA. The proposed rule also provides for early termination of a SCOA. The Exchange believes the early termination of a SCOA is appropriate to ensure that orders do not execute when certain conditions occur, and such conditions are generally consistent with existing COA early-termination functionality.
The Exchange again notes that the communication functionality for SCOA is the same as the existing functionality for COA, providing Users with the ability to place a stop-limit complex order if they so choose. When utilizing a stop-limit complex order, Users also have the choice to select the trigger condition for the order and must designate a limit price. Market participants who wish to place a stop-limit complex order have the flexibility to choose one of two types of trigger conditions which, if met, would execute the stop-limit complex order for SCOA processing. The trigger conditions rely on certain option or underlying prices, or index levels. The Exchange believes it is appropriate to use the Market-Maker SBBO for one of the trigger conditions because it will help insulate a stop-limit complex order from being triggered by an inappropriate trigger event (such as one or more customer orders placed at an extreme price) that could otherwise be caused by including non-Market-Maker limit orders into the SBBO. Use of the Market-Maker SBBO as a triggering condition is intended to help avoid cascading triggering events that could result from customer stop-limit complex orders with limit prices that are not necessarily reflective of market valuation. Use of the Market-Maker SBBO will help support greater market stability and execution and provides certain protections to market participants who wish to utilize stop-limit complex orders. The Exchange believes the proposed changes to add stop-limit complex orders and SCOA are not unfairly discriminatory, as the abilities to place a stop-limit order and respond to a SCOA auction message are generally available to all Users. The proposed rule change provides the Exchange with the authority to determine if all Users or only Market-Makers and certain TPHs may respond to auction messages in alignment with Exchange authority for responses to auction messages for COA,
[
35
]
and the Exchange believes it is appropriate to limit responses to Market-Makers and certain TPHs if it is necessary to incentivize those Market-Makers or TPHs to provide liquidity and further encourage competition. If the Exchange were to limit responses to only Market-Makers and designated TPHs, the Exchange would do so to encourage more competitive responses because such responses will have a greater likelihood of fulfillment in larger quantities when such responses are at more competitive prices.
Additionally, regarding risk controls and price protection mechanisms, the Exchange believes the proposed change would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market
(
printed page 75945)
system, and protect investors and the public interest by providing market participants with enhanced abilities to manage their risk with respect to stop-limit complex orders on the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will protect investors and the public interest because the proposed extension of reasonability checks and the inclusion of SCOA processing with drill-through protection as a risk monitoring mechanism will assist Users in minimizing their risk exposure, thereby reducing the potential for disruptive, market-wide events. The Exchange also notes that the proposed amendment to Rule 5.33(k) to cancel or reject all auction responses to a SCOA in the event that any component or underlying to a stop-limit complex order is halted provides an additional layer of protection to market participants by eliminating SCOA processing when trading in underlying securities is not available. Since the proper functioning of the options market relies on the current price or value of an option's underlying security or index for option pricing calculations, the Exchange believes it is generally appropriate to halt options trading, including orders that would utilize SCOA processing, when the underlying price or value has been halted. SCOA will function in the same manner as COA with respect to these protection and risk mechanisms, as well as trading halts, and the proposed amendments are consistent with Cboe Rules as applicable to COA.
Proposed amendments to Rules 5.34(b) and (c) specifically include SCOA with safeguards that exist for COA. The Exchange believes the proposed change to include SCOA in the auction mechanism types that allow Users to specify whethervolume orexecutions in the various named auction mechanisms will count toward the User's class, EFID, or EFID Group limitis reasonable because orders executed through these auction mechanisms are subject to different protections, such as price improvement requirements, as compared to other order types. As a result, these orders have different risk considerations. The Exchange notes that this functionality is optional, and Users may continue to include executions resulting from these exchange auctions in their risk parameters (as is the case today) if they prefer. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed changes are not unfairly discriminatory, as the risk controls and protection mechanisms that will be applied to SCOA are currently available for other auction types. Additionally, the risk controls and protection mechanisms are available to all Users and applied uniformly to all Users who may choose to utilize enhanced risk parameter settings.
Last, the Exchange believes correcting grammatical errors by (1) replacing “appointed” with “appointment” in Rule 5.33(d)(1)(D) and (2) removing an unnecessary comma from Stock-Option Order in Rule 5.33(b)(5) will eliminate confusion in these provisions.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change is intended to provide market participants with new voluntary functionality to automate a manual monitoring process to determine when to execute an order in the event that a specific condition has been met. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because stop-limit complex orders will be available to all Users and processed in the same manner. A stop-limit complex order is a type of complex order that is intended to achieve the execution of a complex order that Users can achieve today through manual monitoring and order submissions. Stop-limit complex orders offer market participants an automated alternative to this manual process. The proposed rule change provides all Users with the ability to submit a stop-limit complex order, which will be processed through SCOA once the trigger condition for the order has been met. Use of a stop-limit complex order (as well as the trigger condition) will be voluntary and within the discretion of a User, and a User may continue to manage complex orders to achieve an execution of a complex order under certain conditions in the same manner they do today. Additionally, SCOA messaging for an order will be sent to all Users who are recipients of auction messaging data, and all eligible Users generally may submit responses to the auction if they so choose. Furthermore, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because the proposed changes apply existing risk controls, which are available to all Members, to SCOA in the same way such controls currently apply to COA.
The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, as the proposed rule changes apply only to a permissible User order instruction regarding how the Exchange will handle and then execute an order. Stop-limit complex orders extend functionality that is available today on the Exchange in stop-limit orders for simple orders to complex orders, and SCOA will utilize certain COA functionality that is currently used on the Exchange. There is no burden on intermarket competition because other exchanges may pursue their own version of a SCOA. The extension of existing functionality to SCOA also includes risk controls, and the Exchange believes that the proposed changes with respect to its Risk Monitor Mechanism will help promote fair and orderly markets by applying existing controls that help prevent erroneous executions, such as buy strategy parameters that may cancel or reject an order executed outside of an acceptable price range. Additionally, to the extent that the proposed changes may make the Exchange a more attractive trading venue for market participants on other exchanges, such market participants may elect to become Exchange market participants.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
IV. Discussion and Commission Findings
After careful review, the Commission finds that the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 2, is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a national securities exchange.
[
36
]
In particular, the Commission finds that the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 2, is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
37
]
which requires, among other things, that the rules of a national securities exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to remove impediments to and perfect the
(
printed page 75946)
mechanism of a free and open market, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest; and not be designed to regulate by virtue of any authority conferred by the Act matters not related to the purposes of the Act or the administration of the exchange.
As discussed above, the proposal will establish a new order type, stop-limit complex orders, and a new electronic auction mechanism, the SCOA, that is designed to facilitate the execution of stop-limit complex orders.
[
38
]
Stop-limit complex orders could help market participants manage risk by allowing them to close an existing position upon the occurrence of a specific triggering event without monitoring the market to determine whether the trigger condition has occurred. In addition, stop-limit complex orders may help market participants manage their complex order exposure more efficiently by allowing them to transact the long and short leg(s) of a complex strategy simultaneously using a single stop-limit complex order, rather than managing the component legs of the complex strategy individually.
[
39
]
All triggered stop-limit complex orders will be processed in a SCOA.
[
40
]
Multiple stop-limit complex orders in the same complex strategy that are triggered by the same event will be processed in the same SCOA, which should enable efficient processing of SCOA orders.
[
41
]
Multiple stop-limit complex orders in the same complex strategy but with different trigger events will be processed as separate SCOAs.
[
42
]
The process in proposed Exchange Rule 5.33(d)(2)(A) for soliciting responses to a SCOA will be the same as the existing process for soliciting responses to a COA, with auction messages sent to all subscribers to the Exchange's data feeds that deliver auction messages.
[
43
]
In addition, consistent with the COA process, the Exchange proposes to permit multiple SCOAs in the same complex strategy to be processed concurrently.
[
44
]
The process for submitting Auction Responses to the proposed SCOA is substantively identical to the process for submitting Auction Responses to the COA.
[
45
]
Consistent with the COA auction process, the Exchange will determine on a class-by-class basis whether (1) all Users or (2) Market-Makers with an appointment in the class and Trading Permit Holders (“TPHs”) acting as agent for orders resting at the top of the COB in the relevant complex strategy may submit responses to the SCOA during the Response Time Interval.
[
46
]
The Response Time Interval for the SCOA, which the Exchange may determine on a class-by-class basis, and which may not exceed 1,000 milliseconds, is the same as the Response Time Interval for the COA.
[
47
]
At the conclusion of the SCOA Response Time Interval, SCOA order(s) will be executed, in whole or in part, against Auction Responses and unrelated orders resting in the COB according to an algorithm that maximizes executed volume.
[
48
]
The first phase of the allocation algorithm will allocate Auction Responses and unrelated orders on the COB to SCOA orders by matching the least to most aggressively priced SCOA orders to contra-side interest, filling the best-priced orders last in an attempt to maximize execution quantity.
[
49
]
Maximizing the volume of contracts executed will protect investors and the public interest because such an allocation is consistent with the objectives of market participants that will use stop-limit complex orders to manage and reduce the risk of loss by closing existing positions. According to the Exchange, these market participants prioritize fulfillment of their orders over the execution price of the transaction.
[
50
]
The second phase of the SCOA allocation algorithm will use the Price-Time allocation algorithm in Exchange Rule 5.32(a)(1)(A) to redistribute Auction Responses and orders on the COB that were matched to SCOA orders during first phase of SCOA processing.
[
51
]
The Exchange states that the two-phase SCOA allocation algorithm is designed to maximize execution quantity while also providing price-improvement opportunities, if possible, for stop-limit complex order customers and ensuring that more aggressively priced orders are filled.
[
52
]
If SCOA Auction Responses exceed the total quantity of the SCOA order(s), after maximizing executed volume and optimizing price-improvement opportunities, the remaining SCOA Auction Responses will be allocated using price time priority.
[
53
]
Upon completion of the initial SCOA, unfilled order(s) will iterate through additional SCOAs at incrementally more
(
printed page 75947)
aggressive starting prices, determined as the least aggressive of the previous auction price plus the Exchange default complex drill-through increment, the most aggressive limit price of the complex orders in the SCOA, or the opposite side SBBO, until (a) all orders are filled, or (b) the most aggressive limit price or the then-current opposite-side SBBO price has been used as the last auction start price.
[
54
]
The additional iterations will protect investors and the public interest by helping to ensure that as many stop-limit complex orders as possible are executed in the SCOA. At the end of SCOA iterations, the System enters any unexecuted SCOA orders into the COB, if eligible, and cancels any unexecuted SCOA orders that are not eligible for entry into the COB, subject to the User's instructions.
[
55
]
Complex orders resting in the COB may execute pursuant to Exchange Rule 5.33(e) following evaluation pursuant to paragraph Exchange Rule 5.33(i) and remain in the COB until they execute or are cancelled.
[
56
]
Executions in the SCOA will comply with the requirements of Exchange Rule 5.33(f)(2)(A).
[
57
]
including the complex order priority requirements in Exchange Rule 5.33(f)(2)(A)(iv).
[
58
]
These requirements will help to ensure that executions in the SCOA respect the priority of interest, including Priority Customer interest, on the Exchange's Simple Book. In addition, the SCOA will terminate early when the System receives an order in a leg of a stop-limit complex order that would (i) post to the Complex Book on the same side as the order(s) that initiated the SCOA and at a price better than the limit price of any of the orders in the SCOA; (ii) improve the SBBO on the same side as the SCOA order to a price better than the limit price of any of the orders in the SCOA; or (iii) join or improve the SBBO on the same side as the order that initiated the SCOA to a price equal to the limit price of any of the orders in the SCOA and cause any component of the SBBO to be represented by a Priority Customer.
[
59
]
These early termination provisions are similar to the COA early termination provisions in Exchange Rule 5.33(d)(3) (which will be renumbered as Exchange Rules 5.33(d)(1)(C)) and should help to protect the priority of interest on the Simple Book and in the COB, including Priority Customer interest. If the SCOA terminates early, SCOA order(s) will be filled to the extent permitted before entry into the COB, if eligible.
[
60
]
Consistent with the early termination policies applicable to the COA, a pattern or practice of submitting orders that cause the SCOA to end early will be deemed conduct inconsistent with just and equitable principles of trade and a violation of Exchange Rule 8.1.
[
61
]
The proposal will protect investors and the public interest by applying several existing price and risk protections to orders executed in the SCOA. The proposal applies the debit/credit price reasonability checks in Exchange Rule 5.34(b)(3)(D) and the maximum value acceptable price range check in Exchange Rule 5.34(b)(5)(C), which currently apply to COA Auction Responses, to SCOA Auction Responses. Applying these price checks to SCOA Auction Responses will ensure consistent treatment of COA and SCOA Auction Responses and help to prevent orders in the SCOA from executing at prices that could be erroneous. In addition, the proposal incorporates the SCOA, in addition to the COA, into the drill-through protection in Exchange Rule 5.34(b)(6), which will allow a SCOA to be initiated at a drill-through price.
[
62
]
The proposal also amends Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4)(B)(i) to allow Users to specify whether volumes or executions in the SCOA, along with the volumes or executions in other auctions, including the COA, will counttoward theUser's class, EFID, or EFID Group limit for the volume and count limits that a User may establish under Exchange Rules 4.34(c)(4)(A)(i) and (iii), thereby providing Users with flexibility in applying these risk parameters.
[
63
]
In addition, the proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4)(F) to provide that the System counts individual trades executed as part of a SCOA Auction Response, as well as individual trades executed as part of a COA Auction Response, when determining whether the volume, notional, count, or risk trips limit in Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4) has been reached. Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4)(F), as amended, further provides that the System counts the percentage executed of a SCOA Auction Response, as well as a COA Auction Response, when determining whether the percentage limit has been reached. Accordingly, Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4)(F) will treat COA and SCOA Auction Responses consistently for purposes of the risk monitor mechanism in Exchange Rule 5.34(c)(4).
The proposal also amends Exchange Rule 5.31(b)(3) to refer to Exchange Rule 5.33 for a description of how a SCOA, as well as a COA, will operate during a limit up-limit down state, thereby providing clarity regarding the provisions that will apply to a SCOA during a limit up-limit down state. In addition, the proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.25(c) to apply the Exchange's auction response processing to SCOA as well as to the Exchange's other auction mechanisms, thereby providing consistent treatment of responses submitted to the Exchange's auctions.
The proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(a) to add or amend several defined terms. The proposed change to the definition of Regular Trading will treat SCOA auctions in the same manner as COA auctions by excluding both auctions from regular trading. The proposed definitions of Auction Response, Stop Complex Order Auction, and Stop-Limit Complex Order will add clarity to the Exchange's rules. The
(
printed page 75948)
proposed definition of Market-Maker SBBO, as discussed above, will ensure that only liquidity provider quotes will serve as one of the trigger conditions for a SCOA, thereby helping to prevent a SCOA from being triggered by one or more customer orders that could be entered at extreme prices.
The proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(b) to treat SCOA in the same manner as COA for purposes of Exchange Rule 5.33(b)(1) and (2). The proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(b)(1) to provide that the Exchange determines which Times-in-Force are available for complex orders, including for eligibility to initiate a SCOA. The proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(b)(2) to allow the Exchange to determine which Capacities are eligible for SCOA.
[
64
]
In addition, the proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(b)(2)(B)(i)(b) to state that the Exchange may determine that a complex order with Capacity M or N may enter the COB if orders on the same side of the market in the complex strategy that initiated a SCOA(s) if there are “x” number of SCOA(s) within “y” milliseconds, counted on a rolling basis (the Exchange determines the number “x” (which must be at least two) and the time period “y” (which may be no more than 2,000).
[
65
]
The proposal amends Exchange Rule 5.33(k)(2) to treat SCOA auctions in the same manner as COA auctions during a trading halt. Under Exchange Rule 5.33(k)(2), as amended, the System will cancel or reject all SCOA Responses and end the SCOA early if any component of a SCOA order or underlying security is halted. The proposed change will protect investors by preventing an execution of a SCOA Order(s) when the current price of the underlying security, which is necessary to accurately price the option components of the SCOA Order, is unavailable due to a trading halt.
In addition, the proposal updates cross-references and corrects grammatical errors, which should help to ensure the accuracy of the Exchange's rules.

VI. Accelerated Approval of Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 2
The Commission finds good cause to approve the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 2, prior to the thirtieth day after the date of publication of notice of the filing of Amendment No. 2 in the
Federal Register
. Amendment No. 2 revises the proposal to: (1) streamline and clarify the text of the proposed rules; (2) amend the definition of Market-Maker SBBO to include stock-option orders; (3) revise the definition of stock-option order to provide that, in classes determined by the Exchange, conforming and non-conforming stock-option orders will not be eligible for SCOA; (4) provide that a SCOA will terminate early upon receipt of a complex order that would post to the COB on the same side as the order(s) that initiated the SCOA and at a price better than the limit price of any of the orders in the SCOA; (5) provide additional details regarding the allocation of contra-side complex interest to SCOA orders at the conclusion of a SCOA; (6) provide that complex limit orders comprised of legs in different groups of series in a class that are not designated as related groups, and that designate, or default to, the SBBO/trade price trigger condition, will trigger a SCOA only if a complex trade in the strategy occurs at or better than the stop price; (7) state that SCOA order executions must comply with the execution price requirements in Exchange Rule 5.33(f)(2)(A); and (8) provide additional discussion to support the proposal.
Amendment No. 2 raises no novel regulatory issues that have not previously been subject to comment and, without altering the purpose of the proposal, strengthens the proposal by providing additional clarity and support, including by providing additional details regarding the allocation of interest at the conclusion of a SCOA. Further, the proposed changes in Amendment No. 2 should help to ensure that the Exchange's rules accurately reflect the operation of the SCOA. Accordingly, for the reasons discussed above, the Commission finds good cause, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,

to approve the proposed rule change, as modified by Amendment No. 2, on an accelerated basis.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106936; File No. SR-NASDAQ-2026-099]
November 19, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 13, 2026, The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Equity 4 to allow for certain orders entered through the OUCH and FLITE protocols to be automatically repriced. While these amendments are effective upon filing, the Exchange has designated the proposed amendments to be operative during the first half of 2027.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​nasdaq/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Equity 4
[
3
]
to allow certain orders submitted through the OUCH
[
4
]
and FLITE
[
5
]
order entry protocols to be automatically repriced by the Exchange, pursuant to participants' instructions. The Exchange proposes to implement this enhanced functionality during the first half of 2027.
Equity 4, Rule 4120 (Limit Up-Limit Down Plan and Trading Halts)
Currently, Rule 4120(b)(1)(C)(ii)(e)(2) states that both displayable and non-displayable incoming limit-priced interest to buy (sell) that is priced above (below) the Upper (Lower) Price Band shall be repriced to the Upper (Lower) Price Band. Rule 4120(b)(1)(C)(ii)(e)(2)(a) states that for limit-priced orders entered via the OUCH or FLITE protocol, which are not assigned a Managed Pegging, Discretionary, or Reserve Order Attribute, the order shall be repriced upon entry only if the Price Bands are such that the price of the limit-priced interest to buy (sell) would be above (below) the upper (lower) Price Band. The Exchange proposes to add a new paragraph (iii) to Rule 4120(b)(1)(C)(ii)(e)(2)(a) specifying that, once an order has had its price adjusted by the Exchange system pursuant to 4120(b)(1)(C)(ii)(e)(2)(a), if the Price Bands move such that the price of the order to buy (sell) would be below (above) the upper (lower) Price Band, the order will continue to be repriced
(
printed page 75928)
either to its original limit price or to the new price bands, whichever is less aggressive.
Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(1) (Price to Comply Order Type)
Currently, Rule 4702(b)(1) specifies the behavior of Price to Comply Orders. Rule 4702(b)(1)(B) provides that if a Price to Comply Order entered through OUCH or FLITE, during Market Hours the Price to Comply Order may be adjusted in the following manner after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book:
If the entered limit price of the Price to Comply Order crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Price to Comply Order could be displayed at a price at or closer to its entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on its choice.
[
6
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Price to Comply Order or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
If the entered limit price of the Price to Comply Order locked a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order will be adjusted after initial entry only as follows. If the entered limit price would no longer lock a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, may be cancelled back to the Participant, or may be ranked and displayed at its original entered limit price, depending on the Participant's choice. A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Price to Comply Order, cancelling it, or allowing it to be displayed is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders. If the Price to Comply Order is ranked and displayed at its original entered limit price, it will receive a new timestamp, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (Rule 4702(b)(1)(B)).
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes to this rule:
1. Provide that if the entered limit price of the Price to Comply Order crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Price to Comply Order could be displayed at a price at or closer to its entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the NBBO, depending on the participant's choice; provided, however, that if the quotation of another market center moves in a manner that would lock or cross the displayed price of a Price to Comply Order, the prices of the Price to Comply Order will not be adjusted.
[
7
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Price to Comply Order unchanged, repricing it, or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
2. Provide that the Price to Comply Order receives a new timestamp each time its price is changed.
3. Provide that if a Participant chooses to have the price of a Price to Comply Order adjusted in response to a change in a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order can be repriced closer to its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more aggressive price). However, if a change in a Protected Quotation would require a Price to Comply Order to be repriced farther away from its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more passive price), the Price to Comply Order will be cancelled, instead.
4. Provide that if the original entered limit price of the Price to Comply Order would no longer lock or cross a Protected Quotation, the Price to Comply Order will be ranked and displayed at that price and will receive a new timestamp, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (Rule 4702(b)(1)(B)).
Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(2) (Price to Display Order)
Currently, Rule 4702(b)(2) specifies the behavior of Price to Display Orders. Rule 4702(b)(2)(B) provides that if a Price to Display Order entered through OUCH or FLITE, during Regular Market Hours the Price to Display Order may be adjusted in the following manner after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book:
If the entered limit price of the Price to Display Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Price to Display Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Price to Display Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
8
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Price to Display Order or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes to this rule:
1. Provide that if the entered limit price of the Price to Display Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Price to Display Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Price to Display Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the NBBO, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
9
]
The Order may be repriced repeatedly, but only when it can be repriced to a more aggressive price, until such time as the Price to Display Order is able to be displayed and ranked at its original entered limit price.
[
10
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Price to Display Order unchanged, repricing it, or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders. The Price to Display Order receives a new timestamp each time its price is changed.
2. Provide that if a Participant chooses to have the price of a Price to Display Order adjusted in response to a change in a Protected Quotation, the Price to
(
printed page 75929)
Display Order can be repriced closer to its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more aggressive price).
3. Provide that if the original entered limit price of the Price to Display Order would no longer lock or cross a Protected Quotation, the Price to Display Order will be displayed and ranked at that price and will receive a new timestamp, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (Rule 4702(b)(2)(B)).
Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(3) (Non-Displayed Order)
Currently, Rule 4702(b)(3) specifies the behavior of Non-Displayed Orders. Rule 4702(b)(3)(B) provides that if a Non-Displayed Order entered through OUCH or FLITE, during Regular Market Hours the Non-Displayed Order may be adjusted in the following manner after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book:
If the original entered limit price of the Non-Displayed Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Non-Displayed Order could be posted at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without crossing a Protected Quotation, the Non-Displayed Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on its choice.
[
11
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Non-Displayed Order or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes to this rule:
1. Provide that if the original entered limit price of the Non-Displayed Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation and the NBBO changes so that the Non-Displayed Order could be posted at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without crossing a Protected Quotation, the Non-Displayed Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the NBBO, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
12
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Non-Displayed Order unchanged, repricing it, or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders. The Non-Displayed Order receives a new timestamp each time its price is changed.
2. Provide that if a Participant chooses to have the price of a Non-Displayed Order adjusted in response to a change in a Protected Quotation, the Non-Displayed Order can be repriced closer to its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more aggressive price). However, if a change in a Protected Quotation would require a Non-Displayed Order to be repriced farther away from its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more passive price), the Non-Displayed Order will be cancelled, instead.
Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(4) (Post-Only Order)
Currently, Rule 4702(b)(4) specifies the behavior of Post-Only Orders. Rule 4702(b)(4)(B) provides that if a Post-Only Order entered through OUCH or FLITE, the price of the Post-Only Order may be adjusted in the following manner after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book:
During Regular Market Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may be adjusted after initial entry in the same manner as a Price to Comply Order (or a Price to Display Order, if it is Attributable). Thus, in the case of a Non-Attributable Post-Only Order that crossed a Protected Quotation, if the NBBO changed so that the Post-Only Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on its choice. In the case of a Non-Attributable Post-Only Order that locked a Protected Quotation, if the limit price would no longer lock a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, may be cancelled back to the Participant, or may be ranked and displayed at its original entered limit price, depending on the Participant's choice, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (B). If the Post-Only Order is displayed at its original entered limit price, it will receive a new timestamp. Finally, in the case of an Attributable Post-Only Order that locked or crossed a Protected Quotation, if the NBBO changed so that the Post-Only Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on the Participant's choice. A Participant's choice with regard to adjustment of Post-Only Orders is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
During System Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order locked or crossed a displayed Order on the Nasdaq Book and the Nasdaq Book changes so that the original entered limit price would no longer lock or cross an Order on the Nasdaq Book, the Post-Only Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged or may be cancelled back to the Participant, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
13
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Post-Only Order or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes to this rule:
1. Provide that during Regular Market Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order locked or crossed a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may be adjusted after initial entry in the same manner as a Price to Comply Order (or a Price to Display Order, if it is Attributable). Thus, in the case of a Non-Attributable Post-Only Order that crossed a Protected Quotation, if the NBBO changed so that the Post-Only Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the NBBO, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
14
]
In the case of a Non-Attributable Post-Only Order that locked a Protected Quotation, if the limit price would no
(
printed page 75930)
longer lock a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may either remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, may be cancelled back to the Participant, or may be ranked and displayed at its original entered limit price, depending on the Participant's choice, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (B). If the Post-Only Order is displayed at its original entered limit price, it will receive a new timestamp. Finally, in the case of an Attributable Post-Only Order that locked or crossed a Protected Quotation, if the NBBO changed so that the Post-Only Order could be ranked and displayed at a price at or closer to its original entered limit price without locking or crossing a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the NBBO, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
15
]
A Participant's choice with regard to adjustment of Post-Only Orders is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
2. Provide that if during Regular Market Hours a Participant chooses to have the price of a Post-Only Order adjusted in response to a change in a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order can be repriced closer to its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more aggressive price). However, if a change in a Protected Quotation would require a Post-Only Order to be repriced farther away from its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more passive price), the Post-Only Order will be cancelled, instead.
3. Provide that during Regular Market Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order would no longer lock or cross a Protected Quotation, the Post-Only Order will be ranked and displayed at that price and will receive a new timestamp, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (Rule 4702(b)(4)(B)).
4. Provide that during System Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order locked or crossed a displayed Order on the Nasdaq Book and the Nasdaq Book changes so that the original entered limit price would no longer lock or cross an Order on the Nasdaq Book, the Post-Only Order may remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the best offer or best bid displayed on the Nasdaq Book, depending on the Participant's choice.
[
16
]
A Participant's choice with regard to maintaining the Post-Only Order unchanged, repricing it, or cancelling it is set in advance for each port through which the Participant enters Orders.
5. Provide that if during System Hours a Participant chooses to have the price of a Post-Only Order adjusted in response to a change in the best bid or best offer displayed on the Nasdaq Book, the Post-Only Order can be repriced closer to its original entered limit price (
i.e.,
repriced to a more aggressive price).
6. Provide that during System Hours, if the original entered limit price of the Post-Only Order would no longer lock or cross a displayed Order on the Nasdaq Book, the Post-Only Order will be ranked and displayed at that price and will receive a new timestamp, and will not thereafter be adjusted under this paragraph (Rule 4702(b)(4)(B)).
Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(5) (Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order)
Currently, Rule 4702(b)(5) specifies the behavior of Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order. The Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order is available during Regular Market Hours only. A subset of these orders are Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders. Rule 4702(b)(5)(B) provides that a Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order may be adjusted in the following manner after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book:
The price at which the Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order is ranked on the Nasdaq Book is the midpoint between the NBBO, unless the Order has a limit price that is lower than the midpoint between the NBBO for an Order to buy (higher than the midpoint between the NBBO for an Order to sell), in which case the Order will be ranked on the Nasdaq Book at its limit price. The price of the Order will not thereafter be adjusted based on changes to the NBBO.
Currently, Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order will be cancelled back to the Participant after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book if any of five conditions are met. The second of these conditions is as follows: The Order to buy (sell) is entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint of the NBBO and is ranked at the Midpoint of the NBBO; thereafter, the NBBO changes so that the Midpoint changes and the Order is no longer at the NBBO Midpoint.
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes to this rule as it concerns Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders:
1. Specify that Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders are only available through the OUCH and FLITE order entry protocols. This change reflects existing Exchange functionality that is not currently described in the rule book. The Exchange is here proposing to correct this oversight.
2. Provide that the price at which the Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order is ranked on the Nasdaq Book is the midpoint between the NBBO, unless the Order has a limit price that is lower than the midpoint between the NBBO for an Order to buy (higher than the midpoint between the NBBO for an Order to sell), in which case the Order will be ranked on the Nasdaq Book at its limit price. After a Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order that is entered with a limit price above the Midpoint for an Order to buy (lower than the Midpoint for an Order to sell) is posted to the Nasdaq Book, if the Inside Bid and/or Inside Offer changes such that the Midpoint changes and the Order is no longer at the Midpoint, the Order will either be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the relevant Inside Quotation, depending on the Participant's choice.
3. Modify the second of the five conditions detailed above for when a Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order will be cancelled back to the Participant after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book. Whereas that second condition currently states that “The Order to buy (sell) is entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint of the NBBO and is ranked at the Midpoint of the NBBO; thereafter, the NBBO
changes
so that the Midpoint changes and the Order is no longer at the NBBO Midpoint,” this same condition would now read as follows: “The Order to buy (sell) is entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint of the NBBO and is ranked at the Midpoint of the NBBO; thereafter, the NBBO changes so that the Midpoint
becomes lower (higher)
and the Order is no longer at the NBBO Midpoint.”
4. In Equity 4, Rule 4702(b)(5)(C), the Exchange proposes to delete the sentence that read as follows: “As discussed above, the price of a Fixed
(
printed page 75931)
Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order will be pegged to the midpoint upon entry and not be adjusted thereafter.” The Exchange is proposing this deletion because this sentence would be obsoleted by the changes to the behavior of Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders outlined above.
Equity 4, Rule 4703(d) (The Pegging Order Attribute)
Rule 4703 sets out the Order Attributes that may be assigned to those Order Types for which they are available. Rule 4703(d) sets out the Order Attribute of Pegging. This Order Attribute allows an Order to have its price automatically set with reference to the NBBO, subject to certain conditions. As it relates to Fixed Midpoint Orders, Rule 4703(d) specifies, in part, the following:
Currently, the Nasdaq system will cancel “Fixed Midpoint” Orders in response to changes to the Midpoint.
Currently, after posting to the Nasdaq Book, the price of a Fixed Midpoint Order will not thereafter be adjusted based on changes to the Inside Bid or Offer.
Currently, a Fixed Midpoint Order will be cancelled back to the Participant after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book if any of certain conditions are met, including that the Order to buy (sell) is entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint and is ranked at the Midpoint and, thereafter, the Inside Bid and/or Inside Offer change so that the Midpoint
changes
and the Order is no longer at the Midpoint.
The Exchange proposes to make several changes to this rule:
1. Provide that the Nasdaq system will cancel
or update
Fixed Midpoint Orders in response to changes to the Midpoint.
2. Specify that Fixed Midpoint Orders are only available through the OUCH and FLITE order entry protocols. This change represents existing Exchange functionality that is not currently described in the rule book. The Exchange is here proposing to correct this oversight.
3. Provide that, after posting to the Nasdaq Book, a Fixed Midpoint Order to buy (sell) that was entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint will either be cancelled back to the Participant, or adjusted repeatedly closer to its limit price with changes to the relevant Inside Quotation, depending on the Participant's choice, if the Inside Bid and/or Inside Offer changes such that the Midpoint changes and the Order is no longer at the Midpoint.
4. Provide that a Fixed Midpoint Order will be cancelled back to the Participant after initial entry and posting to the Nasdaq Book if any of certain conditions are met, including that the Order to buy (sell) is entered with a limit price above (below) the Midpoint and is ranked at the Midpoint and, thereafter, the Inside Bid and/or Inside Offer change so that the Midpoint
becomes lower (higher)
and the Order is no longer at the Midpoint.
5. The Exchange proposes to make several non-substantive changes to Rule 4703(d), so that this rule is easier for Participants to follow it and understand it. These non-substantive changes are as follows:
a. Restate in a few places that Managed Midpoint Orders are only available through OUCH, RASH, and FIX. In other words, orders with this specific pegging attribute are available through all order entry protocols, except for FLITE. This is currently stated elsewhere in the same rule (“[Peg Managed Orders] are available through OUCH, RASH, and FIX only”).
b. Spell out that a Peg Managed Order with a Routing Order Attribute can only be entered through RASH or FIX. This is derived from statements, elsewhere in Equity 4, that Routing is only available through RASH, FIX, and FLITE. However, elsewhere in Rule 4703(d) it also states that Peg Managed Orders cannot be entered through FLITE. Therefore, only RASH and FIX can possibly support a Peg Managed Order with a Routing Order Attribute.
c. Spell out that
regardless of the order entry protocol used,
an Order with Pegging may specify a limit price beyond which the Order may not be executed. This is currently implied in Rule 4703(d), because the rule is currently silent as to whether this statement applies only to certain order entry protocols.
d. Spell out that
regardless of the order entry protocol used,
a Midpoint Pegging Order will have its price set upon initial entry to the Midpoint, unless the Order has a limit price, and that limit price is lower than the Midpoint for an Order to buy (higher than the Midpoint for an Order to sell), in which case the Order will be ranked on the Nasdaq Book at its limit price. This is currently implied in Rule 4703(d), because the rule is currently silent as to whether this statement applies only to certain order entry protocols.
e. Spell out that
regardless of the order entry protocol used,
if the Inside Bid and Inside Offer are locked, an Order with Midpoint Pegging that locked an Order on the Nasdaq Book would execute (provided, however, that a Midpoint Peg Post-Only Order would execute or post as described in Rule 4702(b)(5)(A)). This is currently implied in Rule 4703(d), because the sentence that contains this provision does not specify whether it applies only to certain order entry protocols.
f. A few minor grammatical changes that do not alter the substance of the rule.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
17
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
18
]
in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act because it will promote just and equitable principles of trade and remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by enhancing the price sliding functionality available to Participants that enter Orders through the OUCH and FLITE protocols. As described above, the proposal will permit certain OUCH and FLITE Orders to be repriced closer to their original entered limit prices in response to changes in the NBBO, protected quotations, the best bid or offer displayed on the Nasdaq Book, the Midpoint, or the applicable Price Bands, depending on the Order Type, the market condition, and the Participant's instructions. The Exchange believes this functionality will allow Participants to express their intended trading interest more efficiently while preserving the protections built into the Exchange's rules to avoid locking or crossing protected quotations, posting or executing at impermissible prices, or otherwise producing outcomes inconsistent with the applicable Order Type or Order Attribute.
The Exchange also believes that the proposal is consistent with the Act because the proposed functionality is optional and participant-directed. Under the proposed changes, Participants using OUCH or FLITE may configure, in advance, whether applicable Orders will remain on the Nasdaq Book unchanged, be cancelled back to the Participant, or be adjusted repeatedly closer to their limit price where market conditions permit. Providing this choice will help
(
printed page 75932)
Participants select the order handling behavior that best aligns with their trading strategies, while the rule text will continue to specify the circumstances in which Orders will receive new timestamps, be cancelled, or cease to be adjusted. The Exchange believes that this combination of Participant choice and rule-based constraints promotes fair and orderly handling of Orders and protects investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to Fixed Midpoint Orders and Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders are likewise consistent with the Act because they will make the rulebook clearer, more accurate, and more closely aligned with the intended operation of these Orders. Prior Nasdaq and Nasdaq-affiliated filings have recognized that it is consistent with the Act to amend the rulebook to reflect upgraded OUCH capabilities, to describe pegged order behavior by reference to whether orders are managed or fixed rather than only by reference to the order entry protocol used, and to reorganize rule text so that it is more logical and readily comprehensible. Here, the proposed changes similarly update the treatment of Fixed Midpoint Orders and Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders so that Participants can choose cancellation or repeated adjustment closer to the Order's limit price when the Midpoint changes, while preserving the cancellation conditions that prevent those Orders from resting or repricing in circumstances inconsistent with the Order's intended midpoint functionality.
The Exchange also believes that the non-substantive clarifications in the proposed rule change are consistent with the Act because they will help Participants understand how the affected Order Types and Order Attributes operate. Prior Nasdaq and affiliated exchange filings have relied on the same principle when correcting omissions, reorganizing rule text, or clarifying how upgraded order entry protocol functionality operates. The Exchange believes that clarifying which protocols support Managed Midpoint Orders, Peg Managed Orders with Routing Order Attributes, limit price instructions for Orders with Pegging, and Midpoint Pegging behavior will promote transparency and reduce potential confusion, thereby helping Participants select the most appropriate order entry protocol and order handling instructions for their trading objectives.
The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule text corrections are consistent with the Act because they will cause the rulebook to more accurately and completely describe existing Exchange functionality and the operation of the affected Order Types and Order Attributes. In particular, the proposal specifies that Fixed Midpoint Peg Post-Only Orders and Fixed Midpoint Orders are available only through OUCH and FLITE, which reflects existing Exchange functionality that is not currently described in the rulebook. The proposal also clarifies related aspects of Rule 4703(d), including protocol availability for Managed Midpoint Orders, the entry protocols that may support a Peg Managed Order with a Routing Order Attribute, the use of limit prices for Orders with Pegging regardless of protocol, the initial pricing of Midpoint Pegging Orders, and the treatment of locked Inside Bid and Inside Offer conditions. These corrections and clarifications are reduce potential confusion, and help Participants understand and select the appropriate order entry protocol and order handling instructions.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The proposal will not impose an undue burden on intermarket competition because it is designed to enhance Nasdaq's order handling functionality in a highly competitive market for order flow. Nasdaq and its affiliated exchanges have previously explained that changes facilitating enhancements to exchange systems and order entry protocols are pro-competitive because they bolster the efficiency, functionality, and overall attractiveness of the exchange in an absolute sense and relative to its peers. The Exchange believes the same rationale applies here because the proposal will allow Nasdaq to offer enhanced price sliding and midpoint order handling functionality through OUCH and FLITE, thereby enabling the Exchange to compete more effectively with other execution venues that offer order handling functionality designed to give market participants flexibility in posting, repricing, or cancelling orders.
The proposal also will not impose an undue burden on intramarket competition. The proposed functionality will be available to all similarly situated Participants that use the affected order entry protocols and configure their ports or Orders to use the applicable functionality. Participants that do not wish to use the enhanced repricing functionality may choose cancellation or unchanged resting behavior where the applicable rule permits, and Participants remain free to select the order entry protocol and Order Type that best serve their trading strategies. Because the proposed changes apply uniformly based on objective protocol, Order Type, Order Attribute, and Participant instruction criteria, the Exchange does not believe the proposal will unfairly discriminate among Participants or place any category of Participant at a competitive disadvantage.
To the contrary, the Exchange believes the proposal will enhance competition by improving the efficiency and utility of Nasdaq's order handling functionality. The proposed changes are intended to reduce unnecessary order entry and cancellation activity, allow Participants to maintain greater control over whether an Order remains posted, is cancelled, or is repriced, and permit the Exchange to process applicable Orders in a manner more closely aligned with Participant instructions. The Exchange therefore believes that the proposal will support, rather than burden, competition among exchanges and among Participants by improving the choices available to Participants and by making Nasdaq's rules more transparent and its order handling functionality more efficient.
The Exchange likewise does not believe that the proposed rule text corrections will impose any burden on competition. These corrections are not designed to alter the competitive position of any Participant or category of Participants, but instead to make the rulebook accurately reflect existing functionality and to clarify how the affected Order Types and Order Attributes operate. Because the corrections will apply uniformly to all Participants and will not change the availability of the relevant functionality except as otherwise described in the proposed rule change, the Exchange believes they will have no adverse impact on intramarket competition. The Exchange also believes the corrections will support intermarket competition by improving the clarity and reliability of Nasdaq's rules, which helps Participants compare Nasdaq's order handling functionality with that of other venues and select the venue and protocol that best meet their trading objectives.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
(
printed page 75933)
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
19
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
20
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-099 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-099. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-099 and should be submitted on or before December 15, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
21
]
Vanessa A. Countryman,
Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Miami International Securities Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change To Permit the Listing and Trading of Binary Options on Broad-Based Indexes
full_text:
